title: Report the complete copied Nest shutdown modules
body:
## TL;DR

Report the complete copied shutdown modules in Nest. Deslop currently shows only a small shared section even though the two modules perform the same work with renamed hooks.

## Details

The curated Nest example is one module written twice with renamed hook names and minor annotation/comment differences. The report should show the complete copied modules. Instead, both v0.37.0 and the commit shipped as v0.38.0 show only an inner section.

This is a pre-existing accuracy defect, not a regression between the two release commits. The scheduled corpus check catches the missing extent. Its informational-group assertions also incorrectly demand duplicated-code weight and rank from groups that intentionally carry neither; those checks need correction without accepting informational groups as proof of a real copy.

## Steps To Reproduce

1. Fetch the pinned corpus with `node scripts/corpus/fetch-corpus.mjs nest`.
2. Build the release CLI with `cargo build --release --bin deslop`.
3. Run `cargo test --release -p deslop --test corpus_repos corpus_nest_typescript -- --ignored --exact --nocapture --test-threads=1`.
4. Observe the shutdown-module extent assertion fail.

## Details (for AI)

```shell
# environment
deslop versions: adf93d9606fc26bf301dc7385ed89311bfa8af64 and bdcd58b8a37f524abbdf208a9114ad766900de5f
os: macOS, arm64
surface: cli / corpus assertions

# context
corpus: https://github.com/nestjs/nest.git at dfaa376170168d12d9d28bcfe137a9bacce579a3
manifest: corpus/nest.json, must_find_type2 shutdown-hook pair, min_nodes=200
scheduled failure: https://github.com/Nimblesite/Deslop/actions/runs/38613248261

# evidence
cluster id: 187aa7013e4d3d9d
reported inner section: canonical_node_count=81
files involved:
  - packages/core/hooks/before-app-shutdown.hook.ts:53-67
  - packages/core/hooks/on-app-shutdown.hook.ts:49-66
root cause: content call-target guard treats a method rename on an unchanged receiver as unrelated even when a copied explicit contract or positive local type predicate owns that method vocabulary
specs: [FUSED-CONTENT-GATE-CALL-TARGET-CONTRACT], [FUSED-CONTENT-GATE-CALL-TARGET-PADDING], [CORPUS-SCORE-COMPARE]
work branch: fix/corpus-clone-extent
implementation PR: https://github.com/Nimblesite/Deslop/pull/593

# pinning tests
crates/deslop/tests/clone_extent_recovery/shutdown_hooks.rs
  lifecycle_dispatchers_keep_the_whole_renamed_module
  changed_operations_on_the_same_contract_keep_only_the_shared_work
  negated_and_optional_type_guards_do_not_rename_the_receiver_contract
crates/deslop/tests/clone_extent_recovery/grouped_commands.rs
  protects independently judged Cobra factory extent
crates/deslop-core/src/content/call_targets/contracts/tests.rs
  rebinding_or_shadowing_cannot_borrow_the_old_receiver_contract
  an_unrelated_nested_predicate_cannot_qualify_the_call
  failed at checkpoint 32c264a8: value = other; retained stale ownership
```

## Acceptance Criteria (for AI)

- The curated Nest shutdown pair is reported with at least 200 nodes and exactly its two module occurrences.
- The reduced CLI fixture reports one complete nearly-identical cluster, two occurrences spanning Before.ts and After.ts lines 1–27, rank 1, with accurate duplication metrics.
- Changed operations on an unchanged explicit contract, negation, disjunction, receiver reassignment, and lexical shadowing cannot borrow false rename evidence; the genuinely shared interior still appears.
- Informational groups retain zero weight/rank and cannot satisfy curated clone recall or precision checks.
- Independently judged corpus scoring and judged-line coverage do not regress, including the Cobra command factories; unjudged legacy Tornado entries are inconclusive and excluded from the accuracy conclusion.
- Full CI and coverage pass without weakening existing assertions.

## Screenshots

None.

title: Count only chosen duplication types in the total, with optional per-type limits
body:
## TL;DR

Let users choose which types of duplication count toward the total duplication figure, and give each type its own optional limit. By default only Identical and Nearly identical count, so most repos will see a lower total; disabled types appear greyed out in the editor and get no bubbles.

## Details

Today the total duplication percentage includes every type of duplicate Deslop finds except "Same shape, different content". That means looser findings like "Similar code" and "Same behavior, different code" push the total up, even though many users only care about real copy-paste. There is one overall limit (`max_duplication_percent`) and no way to set a limit for a single type.

Wanted:

1. **A limit per duplication type.** Each type (Identical, Nearly identical, Similar, Same behavior, Structural only) gets its own optional maximum percentage. All of them are off by default. Going over any limit that is set fails the run, like the existing overall limit.
2. **Choose which types count toward the total.** In the config file the user turns each type on or off for the total. Identical and Nearly identical are on by default; Similar, Same behavior and Structural only are off by default. Most repos' totals will drop when this ships, and the report should make clear which types the total includes.
3. **Disabled types look disabled in the editor.** Types that do not count toward the total are greyed out wherever types are listed (panels, report, filters), and no bubbles appear for them in the code.
4. **One consistent type order everywhere:** Identical → Nearly identical → Similar → Same behavior → Structural only.

Assumption to confirm: the request named four types; Deslop has a fifth, "Same behavior, different code". This issue treats it as off by default and places it between Similar and Structural only.

## Further UI Changes

- The default grouping should be Clone Type
- The sort order for clone types are: Identical -> Nearly Identical -> Similar -> Structural Only. But, note that similar and structural only should be somewhat greyed out unless the user opts to include them

## Steps To Reproduce

1. Run `deslop . --output /tmp/deslop` on any repo that has both copied code and loosely similar code.
2. Open the report: the total duplication percentage includes Similar and Same behavior findings, with no way to exclude them.
3. Add `[threshold] max_duplication_percent = 5` to `.deslop.toml`: this is the only limit available — there is no per-type limit.
4. Open the repo in VS Code with the Deslop extension: bubbles show for every type, and no type is shown as excluded.
5. Look at the order types are listed in: today it is Identical, Nearly identical, Same behavior, Similar, Structural only — Same behavior comes before Similar.

## Details (for AI)

```shell
# environment
deslop --version: deslop 0.36.0
os: Linux (WSL2 6.18)
surface: cli | vsix | mcp

# scope
type: Feature
affected surfaces: cli, vsix, mcp
related issues: None
```

Current code:

- Total = `compute_repo_metrics` in `crates/deslop-core/src/report_metrics.rs` filters clusters with `ClusterKind::is_clone()` (`crates/deslop-core/src/buckets.rs:52`), i.e. every kind except `StructuralOnly` counts. This filter must be driven by the configured include set instead. All percentage maths stays in Rust ([METRICS-REPO]); per-kind `duplicated_loc` / `duplication_percent` must be added to `RepoMetrics` (wire model in `docs/models/live-ipc.td`, generated — never hand-written) so clients render, never compute.
- Only threshold: `RawThreshold.max_duplication_percent` (`crates/deslop-core/src/config/raw.rs:146`), resolved in `crates/deslop-core/src/report.rs:187`, exit code per [EXIT-CODES]. Per-kind thresholds extend this; defaults are named constants, all unset.
- Display order: `ClusterKind::all()` (`buckets.rs:58`) is `Identical, NearlyIdentical, SameBehavior, LooselySimilar, StructuralOnly`; reorder to `Identical, NearlyIdentical, LooselySimilar, SameBehavior, StructuralOnly`. `html_buckets.rs:67` and every client list must read the one order. `strength()` (`buckets.rs:95`) is the fold order ([CLONE-KIND-FOLD]) and is a separate concern — do not change it without a decision.
- Spec conflict: [CLONE-BUCKETS-STRUCTURAL-ONLY] says structural-only is never duplication and always has zero weight. Allowing it to be toggled into the total contradicts that spec — update the spec in the same change, or keep structural-only permanently excluded. 🛑 Resolve before implementing.
- VS Code: bubbles in `clients/vscode/src/bubble/` (`live.ts`, `inlay.ts`) have no kind filter. Related settings: `deslop.ranking.structuralOnly` and `deslop.diagnostics.severityByKind` in `clients/vscode/package.json`. The enabled/disabled state comes from the server (config), not a client-side calculation.

Proposed config shape (illustrative):

```toml
[threshold]
max_duplication_percent = 10        # existing: limit on the total

[threshold.kinds]                   # new: per-type limits, all off by default
identical = 3
nearly_identical = 5

[total]                             # new: which types count toward the total
include = ["identical", "nearly_identical"]   # default
```

## Acceptance Criteria (for AI)

- With no config, the total duplication percentage counts only Identical and Nearly identical clusters; a fixture repo with Identical, Nearly identical, Similar and Same behavior clusters asserts the exact total, and the exact per-kind percentages.
- The same fixture with `include` set to all clone kinds reproduces the pre-change total exactly (asserted), proving no figure silently moved.
- Each kind has an optional `max_duplication_percent`; unset by default. Setting one below that kind's measured percentage exits with the threshold-breach code per [EXIT-CODES]; setting it above passes. Asserted per kind.
- A kind excluded from the total still appears in the report, but is marked excluded (JSON field and human report), and its lines do not count in the total, per-file or per-folder figures.
- Every surface lists kinds in the order Identical → Nearly identical → Similar → Same behavior → Structural only: HTML report, terminal summary, JSON, VS Code tree, webview filters. Asserted in each surface's tests.
- In VS Code, excluded kinds render greyed out in every panel that lists kinds, and no bubble appears for a cluster of an excluded kind; enabling the kind in config makes its bubbles appear after the live refresh. Covered by E2E tests against the built VSIX.
- All new defaults and thresholds are named constants, configurable in `.deslop.toml`, and carry spec IDs cross-referenced across spec, code and tests.
- Existing tests that assert old totals get new values pinned by new assertions; no assertion is removed or weakened.

## Screenshots

None.

title: VSIX upgrade leaves the agent's deslop-mcp pinned to the old build, so every agent call fails against the new deslop-lsp
body:
## TL;DR

After the VSIX upgrades from one build to another, the agent's Deslop tools stop working. The agent's tool registration still points at the old extension folder, so the old `deslop-mcp` talks to the new `deslop-lsp` and refuses every reply. The error says "reinstall the Deslop VSIX", but reinstalling does not fix it, because nothing updates the registration.

## Details

The editor upgraded Deslop to 0.37.0 today. VS Code now lists only `nimblesite.deslop-live-0.37.0-darwin-arm64`, and its `deslop-lsp` serves `.deslop/cache/deslop.sock` for the workspace. The old folder `nimblesite.deslop-live-0.0.0-dev` is still on disk. Claude Code's user-scope MCP entry still names that folder's `deslop-mcp` by absolute path, and six of those stale processes are running.

Every agent call fails, so agents can neither run the required `find-similar` check before writing code nor read the clusters the editor panel shows. The panel itself works and lists 11 identical, 107 nearly identical and 135 similar clusters. The agent sees none of them.

Related: #558 (the old error named the editor build "unknown"; that part is fixed, since this error names both builds), #523, #276, #468/#469 (versioned VSIX paths).

## Steps To Reproduce

1. Install a Deslop VSIX, and register its bundled `deslop-mcp` with Claude Code by absolute path (`~/.vscode/extensions/nimblesite.deslop-live-<old>/bin/darwin-arm64/deslop-mcp --root .`).
2. Upgrade the extension to a newer VSIX build.
3. Open the workspace so the new `deslop-lsp` starts and owns `.deslop/cache/deslop.sock`.
4. Call `duplicates` (or `find-similar`) from the agent.
5. Observe the mixed-build refusal. Reinstall the VSIX as the error advises; the failure persists.

## Details (for AI)

```shell
# environment
editor extension: nimblesite.deslop-live 0.37.0 (darwin-arm64), only entry in extensions.json
stale folder on disk: nimblesite.deslop-live-0.0.0-dev (not in extensions.json)
deslop CLI on PATH: 0.36.0
os: macOS (Darwin 25.6.0), arm64
surface: mcp / lsp

# running processes
.../nimblesite.deslop-live-0.37.0-darwin-arm64/bin/darwin-arm64/deslop-lsp <workspace> --stdio
.../nimblesite.deslop-live-0.0.0-dev/bin/darwin-arm64/deslop-mcp --root .   (x6)

# claude code user-scope mcp entry
{"type":"stdio","command":"~/.vscode/extensions/nimblesite.deslop-live-0.0.0-dev/bin/darwin-arm64/deslop-mcp","args":["--root","."]}

# call
mcp__deslop__duplicates detail=summary severities=[error]

# evidence
deslop-mcp 0.0.0-dev cannot read the "report/get" reply from deslop-lsp 0.37.0 at ".deslop/cache/deslop.sock": its tool_version is 0.37.0, so it was not decoded. The two binaries are from different Deslop builds — reinstall the Deslop VSIX so deslop-mcp and deslop-lsp ship from one bundle, then re-run the analysis.
```

## Acceptance Criteria (for AI)

- After a VSIX upgrade, an agent's MCP registration resolves to the `deslop-mcp` bundled with the installed `deslop-lsp`, with no manual config edit. Examples: a stable, unversioned launcher path, or the extension rewriting registrations it owns.
- When `deslop-mcp` finds a newer `deslop-lsp` on the socket, the error names the stale `deslop-mcp` path and the exact registration to change, not only "reinstall the VSIX".
- A test upgrades a fixture install from build A to build B and asserts that `duplicates` returns the B report through the agent registration.

title: Different multiline SQL queries score perfect similarity and inflate duplicated LOC
body:
## Problem

Deslop 0.36.0 reports different PostgreSQL catalog queries as `nearly_identical`, scores their token overlap and fused similarity as 1.0, and includes the entire multiline SQL literal in duplicated LOC. The common scaffolding is assigning `CommandText` and binding two parameters; the SQL queries implement different operations and cannot be replaced with one query.

This is related to #534's low-information scaffolding, but demonstrates a distinct impact on multiline string contents and the duplication gate: unshared SQL lines are charged as duplicated code.

## Reproduction

- Repository: https://github.com/Nimblesite/DataProvider
- Baseline main: `62b3062eb50b16e34f3d5094d477f8ba766f8673`; these source spans were not modified by this dedup task.
- macOS arm64, 14 logical CPUs, 36 GiB RAM.
- Released CLI: `0.36.0`; executable SHA-256 `a32d051af8d223a5ab87b8a1c8fffd8ec269fa98ba5ec817b3bf40820afae13d`.
- Existing repo config, default minimum 30 nodes. No added exclusions or hidden findings.

```sh
deslop . --compare Migration/Nimblesite.DataProvider.Migration.Postgres/PostgresSchemaInspector.cs:4252:5324 --compare Migration/Nimblesite.DataProvider.Migration.Postgres/PostgresSchemaInspector.cs:8595:9997
```

The command was run at niceness 10 under a 120-second timeout / 2048-MiB RSS guard and cumulative CPU feedback throttle. Exit 0, 14.860 s, peak 692.52 MiB; no OOM or host crash.

## Exact source pair

`Migration/Nimblesite.DataProvider.Migration.Postgres/PostgresSchemaInspector.cs:113–135`

```csharp
colCmd.CommandText = """
                SELECT
                    c.column_name,
                    c.data_type,
                    c.is_nullable,
                    c.column_default,
                    c.character_maximum_length,
                    c.numeric_precision,
                    c.numeric_scale,
                    c.udt_name,
                    a.atttypmod
                FROM information_schema.columns c
                LEFT JOIN pg_catalog.pg_namespace n
                    ON n.nspname = c.table_schema
                LEFT JOIN pg_catalog.pg_class cls
                    ON cls.relname = c.table_name AND cls.relnamespace = n.oid
                LEFT JOIN pg_catalog.pg_attribute a
                    ON a.attrelid = cls.oid AND a.attname = c.column_name AND a.attnum > 0
                WHERE c.table_schema = @schema AND c.table_name = @table
                ORDER BY c.ordinal_position
                """;
            colCmd.Parameters.AddWithValue("@schema", schemaName);
            colCmd.Parameters.AddWithValue("@table", tableName);
```

`Migration/Nimblesite.DataProvider.Migration.Postgres/PostgresSchemaInspector.cs:213–238`

```csharp
idxCmd.CommandText = """
                SELECT
                    i.relname AS index_name,
                    ix.indisunique AS is_unique,
                    pg_get_indexdef(ix.indexrelid) AS index_def,
                    (SELECT array_agg(a.attname ORDER BY ord.n)
                     FROM unnest(ix.indkey) WITH ORDINALITY AS ord(attnum, n)
                     LEFT JOIN pg_attribute a ON a.attrelid = t.oid AND a.attnum = ord.attnum
                     WHERE ord.attnum > 0) AS column_names,
                    (SELECT bool_or(ord.attnum = 0)
                     FROM unnest(ix.indkey) WITH ORDINALITY AS ord(attnum, n)) AS has_expressions
                FROM pg_class t
                JOIN pg_index ix ON t.oid = ix.indrelid
                JOIN pg_class i ON i.oid = ix.indexrelid
                JOIN pg_namespace n ON n.oid = t.relnamespace
                LEFT JOIN pg_constraint owned_constraint
                    ON owned_constraint.conindid = ix.indexrelid
                    AND owned_constraint.contype IN ('p', 'u')
                WHERE n.nspname = @schema
                AND t.relname = @table
                AND NOT ix.indisprimary
                AND owned_constraint.oid IS NULL
                ORDER BY i.relname
                """;
            idxCmd.Parameters.AddWithValue("@schema", schemaName);
            idxCmd.Parameters.AddWithValue("@table", tableName);
```

The first query reads column types, defaults, precision and PostgreSQL typmods. The second reads indexes, indexed columns, expression-index status, and excludes primary/unique-constraint-owned indexes. Both must remain independently defined and tested. Extracting parameter binding would not deduplicate their distinct SQL literals.

## Observed evidence

Whole-report cluster `39a23feda30750d4`: `nearly_identical`, mass 1116, 32 occurrences. Nearby clusters also group SELECT, INSERT and DELETE command setup (`594251e9def01ce4`, 37 occurrences). Those are distinct database operations, not interchangeable query implementations.

Explicit comparison:

```json
{
  "structural": 1.0,
  "token_jaccard": 1.0,
  "embedding_cos": 0.0,
  "content_measurement": "measured",
  "agreement": 0.75,
  "rename_consistency": 1.0,
  "literal_fraction": 0.0,
  "text_identity": "different",
  "fused_score": 1.0,
  "content_required": true,
  "content_ok": true,
  "admitted": true,
  "classification": "nearly_identical",
  "explanation": "admitted: explicit pair clears every admission guard"
}
```

`literal_fraction: 0.0` and `token_jaccard: 1.0` are particularly surprising given the visibly different raw SQL literals. This report does not claim all remaining DataProvider duplication is false positive.

## Expected / regression coverage

- Compare literal-heavy scaffolding with awareness of distinct literal contents; do not call these two full fragments nearly identical with perfect token similarity.
- Do not count unique multiline literal contents as duplicated LOC solely because the surrounding assignment/binding skeleton matches.
- Preserve detection for genuinely repeated SQL query bodies and substantive duplicated control flow.
- Add a fixture with these different catalog queries plus a true repeated query and verify both pair classification and duplicated LOC.

title: C# named tests already delegate to one helper but still publish as nearly-identical logic
body:
After consolidating 38 expression tests onto one shared parse/evaluate/assert helper, released Deslop 0.36.0 still publishes the one-call named test cases as `nearly_identical`. These cases exercise different behavior (ASCII case conversion, Unicode identity, invalid-date fallback). Their only remaining execution is delegation to the canonical helper. There is no duplicated evaluation/assertion implementation to extract.

Related to the delegation-noise family in #355 (Dart), but this reproducer is C# xUnit.

## Observed cluster

Repository: Nimblesite/DataProvider, branch `refactor/deslop-ten-percent`, based on main `62b3062eb50b16e34f3d5094d477f8ba766f8673`, with the expression-helper refactor in the working tree. CLI binary SHA256 `a32d051af8d223a5ab87b8a1c8fffd8ec269fa98ba5ec817b3bf40820afae13d`.

```json
  "rank": 2115,

  "kind": "nearly_identical",
  "mass": 60,
  "canonical_node_count": 30,
  "occurrences": [
    {
      "path": "Sync/Nimblesite.Sync.Tests/LqlExpressionEvaluatorTests.cs",
      "start_byte": 425,
      "end_byte": 696,

      "end_line": 22,

    },

      "hidden": false
    },
    {

      "hidden": false
    }
  ],

  "occurrence_count": 3,
  "occurrences_truncated": false

```

### Sync/Nimblesite.Sync.Tests/LqlExpressionEvaluatorTests.cs

```csharp
#region LqlExpressionEvaluator Direct Tests

    [Fact]
    public void Upper_TransformsToUppercase() =>
        LqlExpressionAssertions.EvaluatesTo(
            json: """{"Name":"alice"}""",
            expression: "upper(Name)",
            expected: "ALICE"
        );
```

### Sync/Nimblesite.Sync.Tests/LqlMappingCornerCaseTests.cs

```csharp
#region Special Characters and Unicode

    [Fact]
    public void LqlTransform_UnicodeCharacters_Preserved() =>
        LqlExpressionAssertions.EvaluatesTo(
            json: """{"Name":"日本語テスト"}""",
            expression: "Name",
            expected: "日本語テスト"
        );
```

### Sync/Nimblesite.Sync.Tests/LqlMappingCornerCaseTests.cs

```csharp
#region Date Transform Edge Cases

    [Fact]
    public void DateFormat_InvalidDate_ReturnsOriginal() =>
        LqlExpressionAssertions.EvaluatesTo(
            json: """{"Date":"not-a-date"}""",
            expression: "dateFormat(Date, 'yyyy-MM-dd')",
            expected: "not-a-date"
        );
```

## Canonical implementation

```csharp
internal static void EvaluatesTo(string json, string expression, string expected)
{
    using var source = JsonDocument.Parse(json: json);
    var result = LqlExpressionEvaluator.Evaluate(expression: expression, source: source.RootElement);
    Assert.Equal(expected: expected, actual: result);
}
```

Reproduce with `deslop . --notext --nohtml --no-color` under a 120-second/2-GiB watchdog. Inspect the cluster and exact source spans above. The full repository report after this change is 38.881199% (45227/116321 LOC); that entire percentage is **not** attributed to this small false positive. Concurrent release-tool edits also affect whole-repository before/after totals, so they are not an isolated measurement of this refactor.

Expected: recognize already-delegated named test cases as low-information scaffolding; preserve findings for copied multi-statement test logic and duplicate helper bodies. The individual test names and all input/expected triples are intentionally retained for diagnosis. Do not require collapsing distinct cases or weakening assertions to eliminate this finding.

title: CLI 0.36.0 scan bursts across 8–11 cores; expose a consistent worker budget
body:
Released CLI 0.36.0 can briefly consume 8–11 logical cores when scanning DataProvider. A supported CLI-wide concurrency limit is needed for safe use alongside an IDE/build. This is active-scan evidence, not a claim of an idle loop or OOM.

## Reproduction and provenance

- macOS arm64, 14 logical CPUs, 36 GiB RAM.
- Repository: Nimblesite/DataProvider, main `62b3062eb50b16e34f3d5094d477f8ba766f8673`, unchanged committed scan scope.
- Released v0.36.0 macOS arm64 binary SHA256 `a32d051af8d223a5ab87b8a1c8fffd8ec269fa98ba5ec817b3bf40820afae13d`; archive verified against release checksum.
- Command: `RAYON_NUM_THREADS=2 nice -n 10 deslop . --notext --nohtml --no-color`; repeat with `--no-incremental` for cold measurement.
- Run under an external 120-second/2048-MiB process-tree watchdog, sampling cumulative process CPU and RSS approximately every 250 ms. Do not run unbounded on a busy machine.

| Run | Wall seconds | Peak RSS MiB | Sampled peak CPU % (100 = one core) | CPU seconds |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Warm, priority only | 12.819 | 751.92 | 821.62 | 20.88 |
| Warm, external duty-cycle throttle | 14.211 | 738.59 | 1125.62 | 20.79 |
| Cold, external duty-cycle throttle | 16.102 | 819.11 | 1119.94 | 24.38 |

The external throttle pauses only the launched CLI PID after its cumulative CPU budget exceeds approximately two cores; it limits average use, not sub-second bursts. Sampling is approximate and can miss shorter peaks. All runs exited 0; none hit the watchdog. Warm/cold/throttled reports have identical metrics and cluster membership: 116630 analysed LOC, 45993 duplicated LOC, 39.434965%.

## Source evidence

At release tag v0.36.0, `crates/deslop-core/src/shard.rs` worker_count uses `std::thread::available_parallelism()`, capped by work size; `crates/deslop-core/src/pipeline/corpus.rs` also obtains machine parallelism. These scoped standard-library pools do not use Rayon. Consequently `RAYON_NUM_THREADS=2` is not a concurrency control for them. This is not a claim that the Rayon variable is a documented CLI contract.

Related: #28 introduced LSP resource controls, but the measured surface here is the standalone released CLI. Please expose and consistently honor a CLI worker/CPU budget across parsing and comparison pools, document it, and test it with a multicore workload. Preserve report identity when changing the budget.

A Markdown report and machine-readable measurement evidence are being retained in DataProvider under `docs/reports/deslop-resources-2026-10-04.md`. Existing editor processes were not terminated or altered.

title: Publish the official `deslop` CLI binary on PyPI
body:
## Summary

Publish the official `deslop` CLI binary on PyPI so it can be installed with Python tool installers in addition to the existing Homebrew, Scoop, and direct-download methods.

The PyPI project name `deslop` is already used by an unrelated package, so publish the official distribution as `deslop-cli` while still installing the executable as `deslop`.

Publish platform-specific wheels containing the same release-built CLI binary for the platforms Deslop already supports: macOS arm64/x64, Linux arm64/x64, and Windows x64. The PyPI package version should stay in sync with the corresponding Deslop release.

## Usage

```console
$ uv tool install deslop-cli
$ deslop --version
```

## References

body:
## Summary

Add a `.pre-commit-hooks.yaml` file at the repository root so Deslop can be used directly as a remote hook with [pre-commit](https://pre-commit.com/) and compatible tools such as [prek](https://github.com/j178/prek).

The manifest should expose a `deslop` hook that runs a repository-wide scan equivalent to `deslop .`, uses `pass_filenames: false`, and supports normal Deslop CLI options through `args`.

## Usage

```yaml
repos:
  - repo: https://github.com/Nimblesite/Deslop
    rev: vX.Y.Z
    hooks:
      - id: deslop
        args: ["--fail-over", "5.0"]
```

This would avoid requiring users to define their own `repo: local` wrapper.

## References

- [README: Add it to your pipeline](../blob/main/README.md#add-it-to-your-pipeline)
- [pre-commit: Creating new hooks](https://pre-commit.com/#creating-new-hooks)

title: Pair compare refuses the joined copied run the report renders
body:
## TL;DR

Paste a long copied run's location from a Deslop report into `deslop --compare`, and Deslop refuses it with "unknown pair endpoint", even though the docs promise that every location a report shows is valid input for the compare command.

## Details

Since 0.35.0 the report joins a long, byte-identical copied run that spans several statement windows into one finding, so a reviewer sees the whole copy at once. That is right. But the compare command does not know that joined range. Ask it about the two locations the report just printed and it stops with `unknown pair endpoint "left.ts" at bytes 292..1060`.

The command's own help and the spec say the opposite: the `path:start_byte:end_byte` triple is the one every rendered occurrence already carries, so a caller can paste endpoints straight out of the JSON they just read. A finding the report shows but the engine cannot explain on request is a finding a user cannot check.

Every other finding tried works: an ordinary identical pair, a nearly identical pair and a shape-only pair from `crates/deslop/tests/fixtures/ts-mixed-band` all return a verdict when the compare run uses the same `--min-nodes` as the report run.

## Steps To Reproduce

1. Clone Deslop at `v0.35.0` and run `cargo build --release`.
2. Create the two-file fixture from `write_long_run_fixture` in `crates/deslop/tests/cross_cluster_collapse.rs`: `left.ts` is `LEFT_PREFIX + LONG_RUN + LEFT_SUFFIX` and `right.ts` is `RIGHT_PREFIX + LONG_RUN + RIGHT_SUFFIX`, written into an empty directory `corpus/`.
3. Run `target/release/deslop corpus --no-incremental --embeddings off --output /tmp/longrun/report`.
4. Open `/tmp/longrun/report.txt`: one identical finding, `left.ts:9:31` and `right.ts:9:31`; in `report.json` its occurrences are `left.ts` bytes 292..1060 and `right.ts` bytes 344..1112.
5. Run `target/release/deslop corpus --no-incremental --embeddings off --compare left.ts:292:1060 --compare right.ts:344:1112`.
6. See `deslop: analysis pipeline failed: unknown pair endpoint "left.ts" at bytes 292..1060` instead of a verdict.

## Details (for AI)

```shell
# environment
deslop --version: 0.35.0 (engine at 3937ad45, built from main after v0.35.0; also reproduced with the same source)
os: macOS 26.6 (Darwin 25.6.0), arm64
surface: cli

# context
command: deslop corpus --no-incremental --embeddings off --compare left.ts:292:1060 --compare right.ts:344:1112

# evidence
cluster id: 079073e930b8bef2
occurrence count: 2
files involved:
  - left.ts
  - right.ts
report paths:
  - /tmp/longrun/report.json
key output:
  #1 [079073e930b8bef2] mass=240 occurrences=2 canonical_nodes=240 kind=identical
    - left.ts:9:31
    - right.ts:9:31
  deslop: analysis pipeline failed: unknown pair endpoint "left.ts" at bytes 292..1060

# reading
The occurrence is the joined exact run that [PIPELINE-CLUSTER-SUBSUME-STRADDLE] publishes
(`crates/deslop-core/src/cluster/exact_runs.rs`, PR #570). Its byte range is the union of
overlapping sibling windows, so it is not one of the fingerprinted views the compare path
resolves endpoints against (`crates/deslop/src/compare.rs`). The report renders the union;
the compare surface only knows the windows. Contract: [PAIR-COMPARE-CLI] in docs/specs/cli.md.
The LSP `pair/compare` and MCP `compare_pair` surfaces resolve endpoints the same way and
should be checked with the same triple.
```

## Acceptance Criteria (for AI)

- A black-box CLI test writes the `long_verbatim_statement_run_is_one_complete_clone` fixture, runs the report, reads the identical finding's two occurrence triples from `report.json`, and runs `--compare` with them. It asserts a `PairComparison` on stdout with `text_identity` `byte_identical`, `admitted` `true`, `classification` `identical`, both endpoints echoed with paths `left.ts` and `right.ts` and bytes 292..1060 and 344..1112, and exit code 0.
- The same triples give the same verdict through the LSP `pair/compare` request and the MCP `compare_pair` tool.
- The existing `ts-mixed-band` compare behaviour is unchanged: identical, nearly identical and shape-only endpoints still return verdicts.

## Screenshots

None.

title: Make the LSP refresh-command test independent of the file watcher's timing
body:
## TL;DR

The editor test for the "Refresh report" command fails at random, even when nothing is wrong. The file watcher and the refresh command race to notice the same edit, and the test only passes when the refresh command wins.

## Details

The test edits a file so a duplicate disappears, then asks Deslop to refresh the report. It expects the refresh's reply to report that one duplicate was removed.

Deslop also watches the workspace for file changes. If the watcher reacts to the edit first, it removes the duplicate itself, and the refresh that follows correctly finds nothing left to remove. The reply then reports 0 removals and the test fails. The report is correct either way; the test only checks which of the two found the change.

This happened once on a CI runner for PR #567 and passed on re-run with no code change. It passed 10 of 10 times locally. A test whose outcome depends on timing gives no reliable signal.

## Steps To Reproduce

1. Check out `taxonomy2` at 17cb9b56.
2. Run `cargo test --release -p deslop-lsp --test suite --features deslop-core/live,deslop-lsp/profiling -- editor_non_interference::refresh_command_re_evaluates_the_corpus_after_an_edit` repeatedly on a loaded Linux machine, or under `cargo llvm-cov` as CI does.
3. Some runs fail with `editing Alpha.cs away from Beta.cs must drop the clone on refresh`, and the reply shows `clustersRemoved: 0` at `generation: 3`.

## Details (for AI)

```shell
# environment
deslop --version: 0.0.0-dev (taxonomy2 @ 17cb9b56)
os: ubuntu-latest (GitHub Actions), instrumented release build
surface: repo

# context
command: make coverage-run  (cargo llvm-cov --release --workspace --all-targets)

# evidence
failing test: crates/deslop-lsp/tests/editor_non_interference.rs:290
run: https://github.com/Nimblesite/Deslop/actions/runs/36078940505 (attempt 1 failed, attempt 2 passed)
key output:
  {"result":{"clustersAdded":0,"clustersRemoved":0,"clustersUpdated":0,"command":"deslop.lsp.refreshReport","generation":3,...}}
files involved:
  - crates/deslop-lsp/tests/editor_non_interference.rs (refresh_command_re_evaluates_the_corpus_after_an_edit, wait_for_clusters)
  - crates/deslop-lsp/src/commands.rs (refresh_report: delta against the report current when it takes the session lock)
  - crates/deslop-lsp/src/file_watch.rs (LiveWatcher started on the workspace root)
  - crates/deslop-core/src/live/debouncer.rs (QUIET_MS = 250)
```

Generation 3 with an empty delta means an intermediate pass (the watcher's incremental pass after the 250 ms quiet window, or a late cold pass) published the edit as generation 2 before `refresh_full` took the session lock. `wait_for_clusters` also polls with `thread::sleep(500ms)`, which is a timing dependency in its own right.

## Acceptance Criteria (for AI)

- `refresh_command_re_evaluates_the_corpus_after_an_edit` is deterministic: its outcome does not depend on whether the watcher or the refresh command observes the edit first.
- The test still proves the refresh re-evaluates the corpus. After the edit and the refresh, no visible cluster names `Alpha.cs`, and the removal of the Alpha/Beta clone is reported exactly once across the watcher delta and the refresh reply.
- No `sleep`-based waits remain in the test path.

## Screenshots

None.

title: Informational grouping judges every pair of a shape family the content gate already refused, 1.6 M measurements for an empty listing
body:
## TL;DR

After #565, a file of 400 look-alike functions still spends 4 s of a 9 s scan judging 1.6 million pairs for the "same shape, different content" listing, and every one of those judgements is discarded because no group qualifies. The per-pair work is now genuine content measurement, so the remaining cost is the pairwise design of the informational grouping itself, not a lookup.

## Details

Deslop lists functions that share a shape but not their content as information, beside the real duplicates. To decide which members of a shape family belong in that listing it compares every member with every other member: a family of 400 functions is 79,800 comparisons, and it does that for every reference in turn, so each pair is judged twice. The `ledger.js` fixture holds ten such families, and the engine judges about 1.6 million pairs, measures the content of each, and then produces no listing at all, because none of the groups it builds qualifies for the report.

I expected the count-bound check that guards this pass to skip a family that cannot reach the report. It lets these families through: it asks only whether two same-hash members differ in source text, which every pair here does (the functions differ in their literals), so every family is judged in full. The pre-check is cheap and the judging is not.

This is the part of #565 that an index cannot fix: the lookup inside each judgement is now bounded, and the time that remains is the measurement itself, multiplied by the number of pairs. A large, real repository with big families of similar functions pays it on every scan.

## Steps To Reproduce

1. Clone the repository and check out branch `taxonomy2` at commit 8dc039e8 or later.
2. Run `cargo build --release --bin deslop`.
3. Run `mkdir -p /tmp/ledger && cp crates/deslop/tests/fixtures/javascript-minified-bundle/ledger.js /tmp/ledger/`.
4. Run `time target/release/deslop /tmp/ledger --output /tmp/ledger-report --no-incremental --embeddings off --min-nodes 8 --log-to-console --log-level info`.
5. Read the log: `informational count-bound workload families=10 eligible=10 skipped=0`, then `ranked clusters built total=0 input_total=10 dropped_below_min_members=10`, then `cluster stage complete stage="ranked_build" ... elapsed_ms≈4100`.

## Details (for AI)

```shell
# environment
deslop --version: 0.0.0-dev (branch taxonomy2, commit 8dc039e8)
os: macOS 26.6.2 (Darwin 25.6.0), Apple silicon
surface: cli

# context
command: target/release/deslop /tmp/ledger --output /tmp/ledger-report --no-incremental --embeddings off --min-nodes 8 --no-color --log-to-console --log-level info

# evidence
fixture: crates/deslop/tests/fixtures/javascript-minified-bundle/ledger.js (400 functions, 10 shapes, 798,000 Merkle-equal pairs)
release wall: 9.37 s; ranked_build elapsed_ms=4139; pair_content_gate elapsed_ms=3866
key log lines:
  informational count-bound workload families=10 eligible=10 skipped=0
  ranked clusters built total=0 input_total=10 dropped_below_min_members=10 largest_mass=0
hot stack (macOS `sample`, debug build, 5,731 of 5,796 samples under ranked_clusters):
  pipeline/session/information.rs ranked_clusters (KindFilter { clones: false })
  -> cluster.rs build_ranked_fused_clusters -> build_fused_cluster -> KindFilter::groups -> ClusterKindMeasurer::groups
  -> buckets/grouping.rs group_members -> reference_groups      (400 references x 399 members per family; each unordered pair judged twice)
  -> cluster_kind.rs pair_kind -> classify_pair -> measured_kind_pair (5,290)
     -> pair_compare.rs measure_axes (3,275) -> content::ContentPair::whole (3,272) -> rename consistency / structural evidence / modal bijection
     -> the rest of measured_kind_pair: token and structural axes (~2,000)
why the count-bound lets it through:
  information.rs may_have_information_pair -> same_shape_may_be_information returns true as soon as one same-hash pair is not an exact source match (same_shape_pair_is_exact); every ledger.js pair differs in literals, so all ten families are "eligible".
  reference_groups never removes informational members from `uncovered`, so every member becomes a reference and every pair is judged from both sides.
related: #565 (the O(n^4) lookup, fixed by [FUSED-SHARED-SUBTREE-INDEX]), #429, #414 (flutter time ceilings)
spec ids: [CLONE-BUCKETS-STRUCTURAL-ONLY-COUNT-BOUND], [CLONE-KIND-FOLD], [CLONE-BUCKETS-STRUCTURAL-ONLY]
```

## Acceptance Criteria (for AI)

- A shape family whose members the content gate has already refused as a whole, and whose informational groups cannot qualify for the report, is skipped before pairwise judging: the `informational count-bound workload` log for ledger.js reports it as skipped, and the report is unchanged (0 clusters, files_analysed=1).
- No unordered pair inside a family is judged more than once for the same verdict: `reference_groups` or its judge memoises by ordered fingerprint-index pair, pinned by a unit test with a counting judge that asserts the exact number of judgements for a small family.
- The `minified_artifact_exclusion` tests and the corpus registers (`scripts/compare-versions.sh`) report exactly what they report today.

## Screenshots

None.

title: MCP cannot request the Identical-code bucket: no kind filter, Type-1 shares severity 'warning' with Type-3, and counts differ from the editor (53 vs 43)
body:
## Summary

An agent cannot ask the MCP for the editor's **Identical code** bucket.

- `duplicates` and `find-similar` have no `kind` filter.
- Every `identical` (Type-1) cluster carries `severity: "warning"`, the same as `nearly_identical`. So `severities: ["error"]` returns nothing, and `severities: ["warning"]` returns about 1,000 mixed clusters.
- The editor view renders the same clusters as a red "Identical code (N)" group. The two surfaces disagree on the count.

## Repro (live index, SharpLsp repo, generation 253)

1. `duplicates { "severities": ["error"], "detail": "summary", "limit": 60 }`
   → `clusters: []`, `total_clusters: 0`.
2. `duplicates { "severities": ["warning"], "detail": "summary", "limit": 1 }`
   → `total_clusters: 1056`.
3. Paging all 1,056 (three calls, each over 100 KB, so each overflowed the client's tool-result limit and was spilled to disk) and filtering `kind == "identical"` with `jq`
   → **53** identical clusters.
4. The VS Code extension's tree showed **"Identical code (43)"** with red markers on the same workspace.

## Expected

- A `kinds: ["identical", "nearly_identical", ...]` filter on `duplicates` and `find-similar`, matching the editor's grouping.
- A severity that tells Type-1 apart from Type-3, or documentation of why they share one. The editor treats them differently; the MCP does not.
- The same count on both surfaces. Otherwise the gap should be explained, for example "the editor hides N clusters overlapped by larger ones".

## Impact

The user asked for "clean up all the identical code". Answering that took three oversized responses plus `jq` outside the MCP. Without the offline filter, an agent would miss or mis-count the most important bucket.

title: rescan is redundant with the incremental index, and its summary reports 0 changes for edits that removed clusters
body:
## Summary

With the incremental index working, `rescan` is redundant — and its `summary` delta is misleading, because by the time it runs the index has already absorbed the edits, so it reports **zero** change for edits that removed clusters.

## Evidence (one session, real edits)

- Before any edit: `generation: 2`, `clusters_total: 2128`, cluster `5e76a5dfab646602` present.
- Edited 5 files + added 1 (Write/Edit tools; no rescan).
- `rescan` → `generation: 26`, `clusters_total: 2126`, and `cluster-by-id 5e76a5dfab646602` → "no cluster with id". But the rescan `summary` said:
  `clusters_added: 0, clusters_removed: 0, clusters_updated: 0, worst_mass: 0`
- `cache_stats` on that rescan: `hits: 485, misses: 0` — immediately after 6 files changed.
- Every later edit (including a `git checkout` restoring 14 files, and new files) showed up in plain `duplicates` / `cluster-by-id` calls with the generation advancing, **without** any rescan.

So the delta is computed against the previous *generation*, which the watcher had already advanced past the edits. An agent reading the summary concludes its refactor did nothing.

## Suggestion

Drop `rescan` from the MCP surface (the index is incremental — the tool invites agents to spend calls on it), or make it useful: report the delta against a caller-supplied `since_generation`, and make `cache_stats` describe the call it's attached to.

## Environment

deslop MCP (`tool_version: 0.0.0-dev`, live index), macOS arm64.

title: duplicates detail:full silently truncates the page (limit 400 → returned 2, no truncated flag or cursor)
body:
## Summary

`duplicates` with `detail: "full"` silently returns a fraction of the requested page. Nothing in the response says the page was cut short, so a client that trusts `page` concludes the corpus has 2 clusters.

## Repro

Live index on a repo with ~2,100 clusters:

```json
{ "detail": "full", "limit": 400, "max_occurrences": 80 }
```

Response:

```
page: { limit: 400, offset: 0, returned: 2 }
total_clusters: 2119
```

No `truncated` flag, no `next` cursor, no `next_action`. The same call with `detail: "summary"` and `limit: 700` returns all 700 — and *does* carry `next_action: "call duplicates with smaller limit, or paginate via offset/limit"` — so the size cap exists, it just isn't reported on the `full` path.

## Expected

Either return the full page, or return what fits **and** say so: `page.truncated: true`, the reason (byte cap), and the offset to resume from. `returned < limit` with `offset + returned < total_clusters` should never be silent.

## Environment

deslop MCP (`tool_version: 0.0.0-dev`, live index), macOS arm64.

title: Live index counts files outside the workspace root in workspace metrics (per_file shows an absolute /tmp path)
body:
## Summary

The live index behind the MCP counts a file **outside the workspace root** in the workspace's metrics. `files_analysed`, `analysed_loc` and `per_file` all include it, so the headline `duplication_percent` is computed over a corpus that isn't the repo.

## Observed

Workspace: a repo checked out at `<repo>`. Scratch file created at `/private/tmp/<session>/scratchpad/codemod-lsp-suite.cjs` (a 200-line Node script, never under `<repo>`, not matched by anything in `.deslop.toml`).

`duplicates` with `include_per_file: true` then returned:

```
files_analysed: 488          # one more than the repo contains
per_file[]: { path: "/private/tmp/<session>/scratchpad/codemod-lsp-suite.cjs",
              analysed_loc: 200, duplicated_loc: 0 }
```

Every other `per_file` path is repo-relative (`src/...`, `tools/...`); this one is absolute, which is itself a hint that it arrived through a different door (probably an editor `didOpen` of a document outside every workspace folder).

## Impact

- `analysed_loc` inflated by 200 → `duplication_percent` understated (18.555% true vs 18.530% reported here). Small in this case, but unbounded: open a large file from anywhere on disk and the repo's score moves.
- Made a real refactor look like it *added* 91 analysed lines, which cost time to chase down.
- A CI gate measures the repo only, so the live number and the gate number drift for reasons unrelated to the code.

## Expected

Documents outside every workspace folder are either not indexed at all, or indexed for their own diagnostics but excluded from workspace metrics (`files_analysed`, `analysed_loc`, `duplicated_loc`, `per_file`, clusters).

## Environment

deslop MCP (`tool_version: 0.0.0-dev`, live index), macOS arm64, VS Code with deslop-live.

title: Prevent nested empty spans from inflating duplicate overlap
body:
## TL;DR

Deslop can count the same code nodes twice when several nested wrappers point to one empty source position. This can inflate a duplicate score and allow a pair that an exact comparison would reject.

## Details

A duplicate score must never claim more shared code than the exact comparison finds. A focused fixture builds two trees that share four code nodes under different outer wrappers. The exact comparison finds four shared nodes, but the shortcut claims nine.

The shortcut is used for findings whose trees are too large for the exact comparison. The small fixture proves its arithmetic is unsafe; it does not establish that a published corpus finding has this exact shape. The fix must keep the shortcut conservative without losing ordinary large-copy findings.

## Steps To Reproduce

1. In this repository, run `cargo test -p deslop-core zero_width_nested_subtrees_are_not_credited_twice --lib -- --nocapture` against the failing test before the fix.
2. Observe `credit 9 exceeds exact 4`.
3. Inspect the large-tree shortcut in `crates/deslop-core/src/overlap/credit.rs` and the test in `crates/deslop-core/src/overlap/tests/exact_bounds.rs`.

## Details (for AI)

```shell
# environment
deslop --version: 0.0.0-dev
os: macOS 26.6.2, arm64
surface: core overlap measurement / CLI

# evidence
fixture: two five-node normalized trees, each with a four-node identical nested chain whose byte ranges are all [0,0); the outer root kinds differ
exact aligned shared mass: 4
credit_shared_nodes before fix: 9
failing test: overlap::tests::exact_bounds::zero_width_nested_subtrees_are_not_credited_twice
file: crates/deslop-core/src/overlap/credit.rs

# impact
The >768-node fallback uses credit_shared_nodes as a conservative lower bound. An overcount can raise overlap above admission floor for an unrelated pair. A proposed exact-bound performance shortcut must not use this value until the lower-bound property is restored.
```

## Acceptance Criteria (for AI)

- The zero-width nested fixture asserts credited shared mass never exceeds exact aligned shared mass; its 4-node exact value remains pinned.
- Existing large-tree positive clone and swapped-order controls remain green.
- A same-shape fixture extended past the alignment cap never reports overlap above what the exact comparison measures.
- The corpus clone-verdict register does not lose a judged true copy or admit a judged unrelated pair.

## Screenshots

None.

title: Identify incompatible MCP and editor builds before decoding duplicate findings
body:
## TL;DR

The Deslop duplicate-finding tool cannot return results when its installed tool server and editor engine come from different builds. It reports a version mismatch without identifying either usable build version.

## Details

An agent asks Deslop to find similar code before editing, as this repository requires. The request fails immediately instead of returning findings. The message says the two installed components disagree, but the editor side identifies itself only as “unknown,” so the agent cannot tell which component to update.

This is a new instance of the mixed-build failure class tracked in #523. That issue covers saved-report parsing; this instance is the live tool-to-editor reply, where a required version field is absent. The command-line detector still runs, but it has no `find-similar` command that can replace this tool call.

## Steps To Reproduce

1. Start the installed Deslop editor service for this repository.
2. Connect an agent to a Deslop tool server from a different build.
3. Ask the agent to find code similar to a Rust snippet with the `find-similar` tool.
4. Observe that no findings are returned and the error says the editor build is “unknown.”

## Details (for AI)

```shell
# environment
deslop --version: 0.0.0-dev
os: macOS 26.6.2, arm64
surface: mcp / lsp

# context
mcp__deslop__find_similar language=rust snippet='fn measure_ordered_views(...) { ... }'

# evidence
key output:
  deslop-mcp 0.0.0-dev cannot read the "duplicates/findSimilar" reply from deslop-lsp unknown (reply carries no tool_version) at ".deslop/cache/deslop.sock": the reply did not decode: missing field `existing`.

# related
#523 concerns a mixed-build saved-report schema parse error; this is a live LSP reply parse error with missing tool_version and existing fields.
```

## Acceptance Criteria (for AI)

- A packaged MCP/LSP pair responds to `find-similar` with a known fixture snippet and returns its expected finding instead of a decoding error.
- A deliberately mixed-build reply that lacks `tool_version` fails with an actionable error identifying both component builds or the exact missing version marker, and tells the operator which bundle to reinstall.
- A deliberately mixed-build reply that lacks `existing` never appears as an empty successful result.
- The same compatibility check applies before decoding every live Deslop tool reply, and a packaging test proves the bundled MCP and LSP use one wire version.

## Screenshots

None.

title: A finding folded into a larger one is lost when the larger one is hidden as noise
body:
## TL;DR

When Deslop folds one finding into a larger one and later hides the larger one as noise, the smaller finding is never given back. If the smaller one was a real copy, it disappears from the report and from the duplication percentage.

## Details

Deslop often finds the same duplication at several sizes: a precise copy, and a wider window around it. It keeps one and folds the others into it. Separately, just before the report is written, it hides findings that look like noise (data tables, boilerplate idioms).

Those two steps do not talk to each other. If the kept finding is later hidden as noise, the findings it swallowed stay swallowed, even when one of them was a real copy that is not noise at all. The spec already says that a view whose keeper is removed must be judged again; hiding at report time removes the keeper without that second look.

This was caught on the django register: a trial change to how Deslop picks between overlapping views made a wide window of dictionary entries the keeper. It swallowed the judged 48-line verbatim copy in `tests/model_meta/results.py` (lines 356–403 = 482–529) and was then hidden as noise, so a CLEARLY IN pair went missing. That trial change was not shipped, but the gap it exposed is in the current engine.

## Steps To Reproduce

1. Build the current `taxonomy` tree: `cargo build --release -p deslop`.
2. Scan the pinned django checkout with debug logging: `RUST_LOG=deslop_core=debug ./target/release/deslop <django@6ef1f6fbe33e9882f82dae026b527800ecb78c36> --no-incremental --no-fail-over --embeddings off --nohtml --notext --output /tmp/django`.
3. In the run log, collect every `cross-cluster subsumption decision="absorbed"` survivor id, and every `cluster hidden from report` id.
4. Intersect them: 697 hidden clusters had absorbed 2,304 other views, and none of those views is judged again.

## Details (for AI)

```shell
# environment
deslop --version: 0.0.0-dev (branch taxonomy working tree, 2026-09-23)
os: macOS
surface: cli

# evidence — current engine, counts of absorbers later hidden ("noise or role gate")
django:      697 hidden absorbers, 2304 absorbed views
bloc:         45 / 230
zod:          62 / 202
nest:         37 / 177
Polly:        32 / 143
tokio:        55 / 126
FSharp.Data:   1 / 1
most absorbed views are trimmed sub-windows of the same occurrences (re-hiding them would be correct);
the risk is the minority that are a different, precise finding.

# evidence — demonstrated false negative (trial election variant, not shipped)
survivor 2ad743a259dfbdc1 (results.py 301-404 + 405-564, dict-entry windows) absorbed f828efa54b9ae2d9
(results.py 319-404 + 405-530, which covers the judged pair 356-403 / 482-529), then:
  DEBUG cluster hidden from report cluster="2ad743a259dfbdc1" kind="loosely_similar" occurrences=2 why="noise or role gate"
corpus score for django fell 9/9 -> 8/9.
```

Where: subsumption runs at cluster build (`crates/deslop-core/src/cluster/subsume/kernel.rs`, `collapse_cross_cluster_overlap` from `cluster.rs`); report-time hiding runs later in `crates/deslop-core/src/report/hidden.rs::cluster_is_hidden`. The kernel's release rule ([PIPELINE-CLUSTER-SUBSUME-KERNEL]: "A view whose absorber is later removed … is therefore judged again against the views that remain") is not applied when `render_report` hides an absorber. Either hide before subsumption, or carry each survivor's absorbed views to the report and re-judge them (noise filters included) when the survivor is hidden.

## Acceptance Criteria (for AI)

- A fixture where a wide window cluster that the noise filters hide encloses a precise copy that is not noise: the report publishes the precise copy (its files, line spans and kind asserted) and counts its lines in `duplicated_loc`.
- The same fixture's hidden window stays hidden (`clusters_hidden` asserted), so no noise returns.
- The corpus score gate stays at 0 FN / 0 FP on every register.

## Screenshots

None.

title: Live compare-pair rejects a near-copy its own cluster reports as nearly identical (intermittent under load)
body:
## What happened

Under heavy machine load the live pair comparison returned a **rejection** for a pair whose own cluster the same session reports as `nearly_identical`. The verdict is timing-dependent: the same commit gives the right answer on a quiet machine.

Extension E2E test `cluster navigation › one click compares a renamed copy with its canonical and titles the diff with its clone kind` (`clients/vscode/src/test/suite/clusters.e2e.test.ts`) failed with:

```
AssertionError: title ends with the pair's kind: Alpha.cs vs Beta.cs: rejected: pair fails content corroboration
```

The assertion two lines earlier — `cluster.kind === nearly_identical` — passed in the same run. So the report says Alpha.cs / Beta.cs are a near-copy while `compare-pair` on exactly that canonical/peer pair says `rejected: pair fails content corroboration` (`AdmissionFailure::Content`, `crates/deslop-core/src/pipeline/session/pair_compare/admission.rs`).

## Evidence that it is intermittent, and load-dependent

Fixture: `clients/vscode/src/test/fixtures/csharp-small` (Alpha.cs is a consistently renamed copy of Beta.cs). Same commit (`431e64a3`, branch `taxonomy`), same machine, `make _vsix-coverage`:

| run | machine load (1 min avg) | result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | normal | 518 passing |
| 2 (inside `make ci`) | normal | 518 passing |
| 3 (inside `make ci`) | ~12 — a 13-repository `compare-versions.sh` run and a VM were saturating the cores | 48 passing, **this test failed** |
| 4 | ~13 | 48 passing, **this test failed** |
| 5 | ~10 | 518 passing |

GitHub's `VSIX tests + coverage` job passed on the same commit.

The test workspace is rebuilt from the source fixture on every run (all files carried the run's timestamp and matched the source fixture byte for byte), so leftover state from an earlier run is ruled out.

## Why it matters

A pair verdict must be a function of the two ranges and the configuration, not of how busy the machine is. A user who opens "Compare To Canonical" at the wrong moment is told a real near-copy was rejected — a false negative on the comparison surface, and a disagreement between two surfaces of one session.

## Where to look

- The suite waits for the first report and then sleeps (`suiteSetup`: `waitForReport()` + `sleep(2000)`), so under load the comparison can be served while the live session is between states. Which input to `AdmissionFacts::from` differs (content measurement, the content floor chosen by `PairPolicy`, embedding evidence) is not yet known.
- Possibly related: #365 (embedding presence changes the corroboration floors).

## Not caused by

PR #552 does not touch the pair-comparison path; the failure was seen while validating it.

title: data_table_rank reads two fields the report never emits: every cluster reports 0 occurrences and the demotion exemption is dead
body:
## TL;DR

One of the accuracy checks reports a wrong number and cannot tell whether the problem it complains about has been fixed. It says a finding has 0 copies when that finding has 34, and it looks for a label the report never puts on anything — so it would keep failing even after someone corrected the underlying issue.

## Details

The corpus suite includes a check that guards the top of the report. Its job is to notice when a block of raw numbers — a lookup table, a list of coordinates — is ranked among the ten most important findings, because such a block is not duplicated logic and should not outrank real copy-paste.

The check is currently reading two pieces of information that are not there. It asks each finding how many copies it has using a name the report does not use, so the answer is always zero: the message it printed for Hugo says "cluster of 0 occurrences" about a finding that actually has 34. Anyone reading that would reasonably conclude the report contained an empty finding, which is not what happened. It then asks whether the finding has already been marked as a data table, using a label that appears nowhere in the report — the word does not occur once in the entire four megabytes of it — so the answer is always "no label".

That second one is the part that matters. The check has an escape hatch: a finding already recognised as a data table is allowed through. Because the label it looks for is never present, that escape hatch can never open. The check therefore cannot distinguish "this data table was correctly demoted" from "nothing demoted it", which means two things at once — it will keep failing after a correct fix, and if the demotion ever stopped working entirely, this check could not tell anyone.

There is a related question for whoever picks this up. The specification says a visible finding deliberately carries no data-table label at all. If that is right, the escape hatch is unreachable by design and the check should be rewritten to state what it genuinely asserts, rather than reading a field that will never be filled in.

## Steps To Reproduce

1. Clone the repository and run `node scripts/corpus/fetch-corpus.mjs hugo`.
2. Run `cargo build --release --bin deslop`.
3. Run `cargo test --release -p deslop --test corpus_repos -- --ignored --exact corpus_hugo_go --nocapture --test-threads=1`.
4. Read the failure line: it reports `cluster of 0 occurrences` and `categorised absent`.
5. Open the JSON report the run wrote and find the cluster it named. It has 34 occurrences, not 0.
6. Search the whole JSON report for the word `category`. There are no matches.

## Details (for AI)

```shell
# environment
deslop --version: 0.0.0-dev
os: macOS 26.6.2
surface: repo

# context
check: data_table_rank
code: crates/deslop/tests/corpus_repos.rs, fn check_data_tables_not_ranked_as_logic (~line 357)
  ~line 369: cluster.get("category").and_then(Value::as_str).unwrap_or("absent")
  ~line 380: field_u64(cluster, "size")
command: cargo test --release -p deslop --test corpus_repos -- --ignored --exact corpus_hugo_go

# evidence
report cluster keys actually emitted:
  canonical_node_count, id, mass, occurrence_count, occurrences,
  occurrences_total, occurrences_truncated, rank, rank_band

measured over a real hugo report (4226 clusters, 4178138 bytes):
  clusters carrying `size`:     0 of 4226   -> field_u64(.., "size") is always 0
  clusters carrying `category`: 0 of 4226   -> unwrap_or("absent") always wins
  occurrences of the string "category" in the whole report: 0
  the correct field is `occurrence_count`; top-10 values are 98,43,67,24,47,27,60,18,15,34

cluster id: f88c8af320ac7e79
occurrence count: 34 (the check reported 0)
files involved:
  - internal/warpc/js/renderkatex.bundle.js

key output:
  data_table_rank: rank 9: cluster of 0 occurrences is 96% numeric/separator characters
  — a data table — but is categorised `absent`, so it ranks at full logic weight.

consequence: `category != "data"` is unconditionally true, so the demotion exemption is
dead code. The check cannot separate a correctly demoted data table from one that was
never demoted, and a regression that removed the demotion entirely would not change its
output.

# scope
type: Bug
affected surfaces: ci
spec: docs/specs/corpus.md [CORPUS-PRECISION] — "any visible closure component keeps its
  full mass and carries no data category", which if intended makes the exemption
  unreachable by design; code, spec and test must agree.
related issues: #439 (the same shape: a corpus check that cannot see what it claims to check)
```

## Acceptance Criteria (for AI)

- The failure message reports the cluster's real occurrence count. For `gohugoio/hugo` at `57a784e027a2`, the flagged cluster reports 34, never 0.
- A test drives the check against a report whose cluster carries a known occurrence count and asserts that number appears in the message, so renaming the field cannot silently return 0 again.
- The check can distinguish a demoted data table from an undemoted one: a report in which the data table is correctly demoted does not produce a `data_table_rank` failure, and one in which it is not does. A test asserts both directions — the negative case is the one that is currently impossible.
- `docs/specs/corpus.md` [CORPUS-PRECISION] and `check_data_tables_not_ranked_as_logic` agree on whether a visible cluster can carry a data category. If the spec's position stands, the check no longer reads a field that is never emitted, and its wording states what it actually asserts.
- No other corpus check reads a cluster field absent from the rendered report; a test enumerates the fields the checks read against the fields a report emits.

## Screenshots

None.

title: Class-nested pytest fixtures are reported as duplicates
body:
## TL;DR

Deslop reports ordinary pytest fixtures as duplicate code whenever they are written inside a test class. It correctly stays quiet about the same fixtures written at the top of a file. Since grouping fixtures into classes is normal Python practice, whole test suites get flagged for duplication that is not there.

## Details

Deslop knows that pytest fixtures repeat themselves by design — every fixture in a suite opens a database session the same way — and it deliberately keeps quiet about them so the report is not swamped by findings nobody would act on.

That only works for fixtures written at the top level of a file. Write the identical fixture inside a `class TestOrders:` — which is how most suites of any size are organised — and Deslop reports it as duplicated code. Nothing about the fixture has changed except that it is indented.

The cause is in how Deslop looks for the `@pytest.fixture` marker: it reads the source lines just above the `def`, and stops as soon as it hits a blank one. For an indented method the line just above the `def` is the method's own indentation — whitespace — so the check stops immediately and never sees the marker sitting one line further up.

Deslop has a second, near-identical check elsewhere that looks for Python's `@abstractmethod` marker. That one was written later, is documented as a copy of this one, and does not have the defect: it skips the trailing whitespace before it starts reading. So one of the two copies was fixed and the other was not.

Per the repository's accuracy rule the defective check has been replaced with a `panic!` rather than repaired, and two tests pin the behaviour.

## Steps To Reproduce

1. Create a Python project with two files, each defining a test class containing an identical `@pytest.fixture` method that opens a database session.
2. Run Deslop over the project.
3. Observe the two fixtures reported as a duplicate cluster.
4. Move both fixtures out of their classes to the top level of each file, changing nothing else.
5. Run Deslop again and observe the cluster is gone.

## Details (for AI)

```shell
# environment
deslop --version: 0.0.0-dev
os: macOS 15 (Darwin 25.6.0)
surface: repo

# context
command: cargo test -p deslop-core --features live --lib cluster_filters::python::tests

# evidence
defect: crates/deslop-core/src/cluster_filters/python.rs
        fn python_function_has_fixture_decorator  (now quarantined)
spec: [CLONE-NOISE-PY-PYTEST-FIXTURE]
sound sibling: crates/deslop-core/src/cluster_filters/polymorphic.rs
        fn python_abstract_method  — uses prefix.trim_end().lines().rev()

pinning tests (crates/deslop-core/src/cluster_filters/python/tests.rs):
  module_level_pytest_fixture_is_recognised   # control, passed before quarantine
  class_nested_pytest_fixture_is_recognised   # the red

key output (before the quarantine was applied):
  test module_level_pytest_fixture_is_recognised ... ok
  test class_nested_pytest_fixture_is_recognised ... FAILED

# analysis
The scan took `source[..function.start_byte()]` and walked `prefix.lines().rev()`,
returning false on the first line that was blank or did not start with '@'.
`function.start_byte()` is the offset of `def`, so for an indented method the
prefix ends "...@pytest.fixture\n    " and `lines()` yields "    " last. That
line trims to empty and ends the walk before the decorator is ever read.
`python_abstract_method` calls `prefix.trim_end()` first and is unaffected.
The callee predicate (text after '@', cut at the first '(' or space, matching a
final dotted segment of `fixture`) was sound and is recorded in the quarantine
comment.
```

## Acceptance Criteria (for AI)

- `class_nested_pytest_fixture_is_recognised` passes: a `@pytest.fixture` on a method inside a class is recognised.
- `module_level_pytest_fixture_is_recognised` still passes, so the repair does not trade one shape for the other.
- A fixture whose decorator block is genuinely separated from its `def` by a blank line is still recognised, and a `def` with no decorator at all is still **not** recognised — the walk must skip its own indentation without becoming unbounded.
- The two scans (`python_function_has_fixture_decorator` and `python_abstract_method`) share one decorator walk, so a future fix to one cannot miss the other.
- An E2E fixture repository of class-nested pytest fixtures reports no cluster across their bodies.

## Screenshots

None.

title: Unrelated struct-array literals report as nearly-identical duplicates
body:
## TL;DR

Deslop reports two completely unrelated lists as near-identical duplicates: a list of test sample files and the list of tools the Deslop MCP server offers. They live in different projects, share no words, and there is nothing a developer could merge. Anyone acting on this finding would waste their time.

## Details

Deslop's own report ranks a finding at position 51 that claims two blocks of code are "nearly identical". One of them is a list of ten small sample programs a test uses. The other is the list of eight tools the Deslop MCP server advertises to editors — its actual product surface, in a different project inside the repository.

The only thing the two have in common is their shape: both are a list of entries, and each entry has a name and two other fields. Every single name, every description, and every value differs. There is no shared code to pull out, and merging them would be nonsense — one is test data, the other is a published interface.

This matters beyond the one finding. Lists like these are the normal way to write a lookup table in any language, so a report that flags them as duplicates will keep producing findings nobody can act on, and pushes the reported duplication percentage above the truth. Deslop already carries a filter meant to recognise data tables and leave them alone; it does not recognise these two.

## Steps To Reproduce

1. Clone the repository and check out `fix/regression-rollbacks`.
2. Run Deslop over the repository root with the default settings.
3. Open the report and find the cluster with id `d7e626730fdddf88`.
4. Observe it is labelled "nearly identical" with two occurrences.
5. Open both occurrences and compare them: one is a list of test sample files, the other is the MCP tool list. Nothing is shared.

## Details (for AI)

```shell
# environment
deslop --version: 0.0.0-dev
os: macOS 15 (Darwin 25.6.0)
surface: mcp | repo

# context
command: mcp__deslop__duplicates { "min_size": 90, "limit": 25, "detail": "summary" }

# evidence
cluster id: d7e626730fdddf88
kind: nearly_identical
mass: 117
canonical_node_count: 117
occurrence count: 2
files involved:
  - crates/deslop/tests/boilerplate.rs:233-284      # [SourceSpec; 10] test fixture table
  - crates/deslop-mcp/src/tools/mod.rs:47-88        # [ToolDefinition; 8] MCP tool registry
key output:
  {"id":"d7e626730fdddf88","kind":"nearly_identical","mass":117,
   "occurrence_count":2,"size_nodes":117,"rank":51,"rank_band":"top10"}

# analysis
Normalisation collapses every identifier to `identifier` and every literal to
`literal`, so `SourceSpec { name: LIT, body_marker: LIT, source: ID }` and
`ToolDefinition { name: LIT, description: LIT, input_schema: ID }` normalise to
the same subtree. The two arrays then differ only in element count (10 vs 8).
`crates/deslop-core/src/cluster_filters/constant_table.rs` exists to suppress
exactly this shape and does not fire. The `nearly_identical` label is
unreachable for a pair whose every identifier and literal differs; the honest
floor for a shape-only match is `structural_only`.
```

## Acceptance Criteria (for AI)

- A fixture repository containing two struct-array literals in different crates, with disjoint field names, disjoint literals and different element counts, produces **no** cluster spanning both at the default `min_nodes`.
- A test asserts cluster `d7e626730fdddf88` (or its fixture equivalent) is absent from the rendered report, naming both file paths.
- A negative-control fixture pins that two genuinely identical struct-array literals **are** still reported, so the fix suppresses shape echoes without blinding the detector to real table duplication.
- The repository's own reported `duplication_percent` drops by the LOC these two occurrences contribute.

## Screenshots

None.
