title: [CLONE-TYPE-TAXONOMY] nearly_identical is assigned on structural overlap alone, with rename_consistency = 0
body:
## Code and spec disagree

`classify_admitted` in `crates/deslop-core/src/pipeline/session/pair_compare/admission.rs` assigns `NearlyIdentical` from structural overlap alone:

```rust
if measured.score.structural >= SHARED_SUBTREE_MIN_OVERLAP {
    return Some(PairClassification::NearlyIdentical);
}
```

It never reads `rename_consistency` or `consistent_rename`. But `nearly_identical` is specified and published as the **Type-2 / renamed-clone** kind:

- `docs/messaging.md:204` — "Type-2 clone | A copy where identifiers and literals changed but the structure did not."
- `docs/specs/pipeline.md:10` — normalization exists "so Type-2 clones (renamed identifiers) hash identically".
- `ClusterKind` carries a `taxonomy` field for `[CLONE-TYPE-TAXONOMY]`, surfaced in tooltips and agent context.

## Evidence

`compare-pair` on cluster `0aa0d20956d67315` (`lang/csharp.rs` ↔ `lang/dart.rs`):

```json
{"classification":"nearly_identical","structural":0.766,"token_jaccard":0.797,
 "rename_consistency":0,"agreement":0.341,"literal_fraction":0.495,"embedding_cos":0}
```

The pair is labelled a renamed clone while the rename evidence is exactly zero. `rename_consistency` here is a computed zero, not an unpopulated default: `agreement` and `literal_fraction` are both non-zero, so `pair_evidence` took the full measurement path (`content.rs:213`) rather than returning `ContentEvidence::unmeasured()`.

The two endpoints are not identical up to renaming — their arities differ — so no rename could relate them.

## Impact

The cluster `kind` is wrong on the wire, in the HTML report, in the VSIX panels, and in the MCP payload agents read. Per AGENTS.md ("Code, specs, and tests MUST agree. Where they don't, STOP and report") this is reported rather than patched.

## Suggested direction

Either gate `NearlyIdentical` on rename evidence (`consistent_rename`, or `rename_consistency` above a configurable floor) and let structural-overlap-without-rename fall to a Type-3 kind, or amend the taxonomy so `nearly_identical` no longer claims to mean Type-2. A test should assert that a pair with `rename_consistency == 0` is never published as `nearly_identical`.

title: [CLONE-NOISE-CONSTANT-TABLE] Per-language const tables in lang/*.rs are reported as the repo's worst duplication
body:
## Defect

Deslop reports its own `crates/deslop-core/src/lang/` modules as a top-`worst`-band duplication family. These are false positives: the clusters are per-language **constant tables**, and there is nothing to extract.

| cluster id | rank | kind | occurrences |
|---|---|---|---|
| `0aa0d20956d67315` | 4 | `nearly_identical` | `lang/csharp.rs`, `lang/dart.rs`, `lang/rust_lang.rs` |
| `b64bef9fb9aff7c9` | 7 | `loosely_similar` | `lang/csharp.rs` +4 |
| `257cc1642e1b6335` | 8 | `loosely_similar` | `lang/csharp.rs` +3 |

## Why it is a false positive

`0aa0d20956d67315` covers `const BINDING_KINDS: &[BindingKind]` plus `const REFERENCE_TABLE: ReferenceTable` in three language modules. The values are entirely disjoint — each names its own grammar's node kinds — and the arities differ (5 / 4 / 6 binding kinds; 6 / 3 / 5 `skip_parent_kinds`). The shared abstraction (`BindingKind`, `ReferenceTable`) is **already extracted**; what remains is per-language data that cannot be shared.

This is precisely the rationale `[CLONE-NOISE-CONSTANT-TABLE]` states:

> A table of distinct named constants is data: there is no shared control flow and no abstraction to hoist, so there is nothing a reader could extract.

## Why the filter misses it

`cluster_filters/constant_table.rs` requires every member's right-hand side to be a plain literal:

> Any right-hand side that is not a plain literal — a call, a name, an attribute, an interpolated string — takes the member out of the shape and keeps the cluster visible.

Here the right-hand sides are const-constructor calls (`BindingKind::new(...)`) and a struct literal (`ReferenceTable { ... }`), so `covers_only_constants` returns false and the cluster survives. The narrowness is deliberate and documented, so this is a coverage gap rather than defective code — but the result is a false positive in the `worst` band, and it inflates `duplicated_loc`.

## Suggested direction

Extend the constant-table shape to admit right-hand sides that are themselves const-evaluable data — const-fn constructor calls and struct/array literals over literals — while still requiring members to differ in raw bytes so a verbatim-copied table stays visible.

title: Mandatory three-line test setup ranks as the #2 worst duplicate group
body:
## TL;DR

Deslop ranks three lines of unavoidable test setup as the **second worst duplicate group in its own codebase**. The three lines create an object and register two files — there is no shorter way to write them and nothing to extract. Real duplicate code is pushed down the list behind them.

## Details

Run Deslop on the Deslop repository and look at the top of the report. The group ranked #2, with a "mass" of 468 across 14 copies, is this, and nothing more:

    let mut registry = FileRegistry::new();
    let left = registry.register(PathBuf::from("left.py"));
    let right = registry.register(PathBuf::from("right.py"));

Every test that needs two files starts this way, because that is the only way to start. The copies differ in the names they use and the files they point at, and those differences are the whole point — each test then asserts something different about the files it just named. There is no helper you could pull out of this that would not make the tests harder to read, and no line you could delete.

Deslop scores this pair a perfect match on every axis: structural 1.0, token overlap 1.0, fused score 1.0, labelled "nearly identical". It reaches that score because the report ignores names and text, so `left.py` and `left.rs`, and `left` and `file_id`, all look the same to it. What is left after ignoring those is a shape that every correct version of this setup must have.

This matters beyond one noisy row. The ranking is driven by copies × size, so a tiny mandatory snippet repeated 14 times outranks a genuine 168-line duplicate that appears twice. A user opening this report is told the worst problem in the codebase is something they cannot fix, and the real finding is below it. The same shape appears at rank #3 (group `1fe73416871563df`, also 14 copies), which is a run of ordinary `assert!` calls — different subjects, different failure messages — that only resemble each other because assertions look like assertions.

## Steps To Reproduce

1. Clone the repository and check out `fix/regression-rollbacks`.
2. Build the analyser: `cargo build --release`.
3. Run it on itself: `target/release/deslop . --output /tmp/deslop-self`.
4. Open the generated report and read the groups ranked 2 and 3.
5. Group 2 is the three-line setup above, repeated in 14 places. Group 3 is a run of unrelated assertions.

## Details (for AI)

```shell
# environment
deslop --version: 0.0.0-dev
os: macOS (Darwin 25.6.0)
surface: cli | mcp
branch: fix/regression-rollbacks @ bd920260

# context
command: deslop . --output /tmp/deslop-self --min-nodes 30
mcp: duplicates(limit=20), cluster-by-id, compare-pair

# evidence
cluster id: 48b34d60495688b6
rank: 2 (rank_band "worst")
mass: 468
occurrence count: 14
size_nodes: 36            # min_nodes floor is 30
```

title: Corpus fetch reads the judging queue as a repository and aborts every corpus run
body:
## TL;DR

`make test-corpus` stops immediately with `corpus manifest is missing "name"` and never runs a single check. The step that downloads the sample repositories treats a settings file as if it were a repository to download.

## Details

The corpus suite is how we prove Deslop actually finds real duplicates in real codebases. Before it can run, it has to download the sample repositories it scans. That download step reads every `.json` file in the `corpus/` folder and expects each one to describe a repository.

Not every file in that folder describes a repository. A few of them hold settings instead. The download step keeps a list of the files to skip, and that list has fallen out of date: one settings file was added later and never added to the skip list. The download step tries to download it, finds it has no repository name, and stops.

Because it stops there, nothing downstream runs. The whole accuracy suite reports a failure that has nothing to do with whether Deslop is finding duplicates correctly, and anyone running it locally gets no accuracy signal at all.

The same "which files are settings, not repositories" list is written down in three separate places in three languages. Only one of them is up to date. Adding a file for one of them silently broke another, and nothing tied them together to catch it.

## Steps To Reproduce

1. Clone the repository and check out `main`.
2. Run `make test-corpus`.
3. Watch it exit after the first step with `Error: corpus manifest is missing "name"`.
4. Note that no test ran — the output contains no test results at all.

## Details (for AI)

```shell
# environment
deslop --version: 0.0.0-dev
os: macOS 26.5.1
node: v26.5.0
surface: repo

# context
command: make test-corpus
failing step: node scripts/corpus/fetch-corpus.mjs

# evidence
key output:
  file:///.../scripts/corpus/fetch-corpus.mjs:65
      if (!value) throw new Error(`corpus manifest is missing "${field}"`);
  Error: corpus manifest is missing "name"
      at fetchRepo (scripts/corpus/fetch-corpus.mjs:65:23)
  make: *** [test-corpus] Error 1

trigger file:
  corpus/judging-queue.json          # keys: why, repositories - no name/url/sha

three copies of one rule, one stale:
  crates/deslop-test-support/src/corpus.rs:34
    NOT_A_REPOSITORY = ["known-failures", "score-thresholds", "judging-queue"]   # correct
  scripts/corpus/fetch-corpus.mjs:32
    NON_MANIFEST = new Set(["known-failures.json"])                              # stale, crashes
  scripts/corpus/target-repos.sh:76
    find ... ! -name 'score-*'                                                   # correct only by accident

pinning test (red, confirmed failing for this reason):
  scripts/repository/corpus-fetch.test.mjs
    [CORPUS-PIN] the fetch skips every corpus file that is not a repository
  run: node --test scripts/repository/corpus-fetch.test.mjs

spec: docs/specs/corpus.md [CORPUS-PIN]
```

## Acceptance Criteria (for AI)

- `node --test scripts/repository/corpus-fetch.test.mjs` passes all three tests; the fetch exits 0 against a `corpus/` tree containing `judging-queue.json` and clones only the manifest that names a repository.
- A manifest that names a repository and carries no `sha` still exits non-zero with `corpus manifest is missing "sha"` — skipping unparseable files is not the fix.
- `scripts/corpus/fetch-corpus.mjs` holds no independent copy of the non-repository list; it and `crates/deslop-test-support/src/corpus.rs` resolve the same source, so adding a file to `corpus/` cannot break the fetch again.
- `make test-corpus` proceeds past `fetch-corpus.mjs` and executes the `corpus_repos` suite.
- The new test is registered in `make test` alongside the other `scripts/repository/*.test.mjs` gates.

## Screenshots

None.

title: Thirty-six rule identifiers are cited in code and enforced by tests but defined in no document
body:
### TL;DR

Thirty-six rule identifiers are quoted in the code and enforced by tests, but no document anywhere defines them. Behaviour is being locked in by tests that point at rules nobody can read, and the project's stated way of tracing a rule to its code and its tests silently returns nothing for all thirty-six.

### Details

Throughout the code and the tests, comments cite a rule by a short bracketed identifier so anyone can search for that identifier and find the written rule, the code implementing it, and the tests holding it. That three-way trace is the project's core convention for keeping documents, code and tests honest with one another.

For thirty-six of those identifiers the written rule does not exist. Searching for them finds the code and the tests and nothing else. Twenty of the thirty-six appear in shipped code, not just in tests, so the gap is not confined to test scaffolding. Some are cited heavily — one appears in five separate shipped files, another in four.

This matters most where a test enforces the missing rule. The comparison panel is a live example: a test actively keeps two commands deleted and cites a rule identifier for why, and that rule is written down nowhere. Anyone trying to work out whether that decision was correct, or whether it may be revisited, has no document to consult and no way to tell whether the test is protecting a considered decision or an accident that has since calcified. The same applies to the ranking rule, which the project's own contributor instructions use as the worked example of how identifiers are supposed to be traceable.

The list also includes identifiers for language handling, logging, reporting context, severity banding, noise filtering and repair behaviour — so this is spread across most areas of the product rather than isolated to one recent change.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Clone the repository.
2. Search the code and tests for bracketed rule identifiers, and search the documents for the same identifiers.
3. Compare the two lists — thirty-six identifiers appear only in code and tests.
4. Pick `[VSIX-PAIR-COMPARE]` and search the documents folder for it — there are no matches, while the code and tests reference it more than ten times.
5. Pick `[RANK-SCORE]`, the identifier the contributor instructions use as their example, and search the documents folder for it — no matches.

### Details (for AI)

```shell
# environment
deslop --version: 0.0.0-dev (workspace build, commit 77b4681b)
os: macOS 26.6.2
surface: repo

# how the list was produced
grep -rhoE "\[[A-Z][A-Z0-9]+(-[A-Z0-9]+)+\]" clients/vscode/src crates/*/src crates/*/tests \
  --include="*.rs" --include="*.ts" --include="*.tsx" | sort -u > /tmp/ids_code.txt
grep -rhoE "\[[A-Z][A-Z0-9]+(-[A-Z0-9]+)+\]" docs/ | sort -u > /tmp/ids_docs.txt
comm -23 /tmp/ids_code.txt /tmp/ids_docs.txt      # -> 36 identifiers

# the 36 orphans (searched against ALL of docs/, not just docs/specs)
[AUTOFIX-CONSOLIDATE-CODE-ACTION] [BRACKETED-ID] [CLI-TEXT]
[CLONE-NOISE] [CLONE-NOISE-DART-WIDGET-SCAFFOLD] [CLONE-NOISE-EMBEDDING-ROLE]
[CORPUS-SCORE-GATE] [DESLOP-LIVE] [FACET-GROUP-BY-SEVERITY] [FUSED-RANK-MASS]
[LANG-CAND-DART] [LANG-CAND-GO] [LANG-CAND-JAVASCRIPT] [LANG-CAND-KOTLIN]
[LANG-CAND-TYPESCRIPT] [LOCATION-LINE-COLUMN] [LSP-CLI-HELP] [LSP-IPC]
[LSP-SEVERITY-BAND] [MCP-JSONRPC] [MCP-ROOT-CANONICAL]
[MCP-TOOL-REPORT-PAGINATION] [MCP-TOOL-REPORT-QUERY] [MCP-TOOLS-FIND-SIMILAR]
[PARSE-FSHARP-NORMALIZE] [PARSE-PHP-NORMALIZE] [PERF-SAMPLE]
[PIPELINE-SIGNATURE-FALLBACK] [PRINCIPLES-LOGGING] [RANK-SCORE]
[REPAIR-COSINE-MERGE] [REPAIR-RENAME-ANCHOR-MASS] [REPORTING-CONTEXT]
[SKIP-BREAKING-CI] [SPEC-ID] [TEST-ONE-BINARY] [TESTS-NO-INDEXING]
[VSIX-PAIR-COMPARE] [VSIX-REACTIVITY-DIRTY] [VSIX-SETTINGS-RANKING]

# 20 of them appear in production source, not only tests
[REPORTING-CONTEXT]            5 production files
[PRINCIPLES-LOGGING]           4
[LANG-CAND-JAVASCRIPT]         3
[FACET-GROUP-BY-SEVERITY]      2
[LANG-CAND-TYPESCRIPT]         2
[LSP-CLI-HELP]                 2
[LSP-SEVERITY-BAND]            2
[REPAIR-COSINE-MERGE]          2
[RANK-SCORE]                   1   # the worked example in AGENTS.md
[VSIX-PAIR-COMPARE]            0 production, 10+ across src and tests

# a test enforcing an undocumented rule
clients/vscode/src/test/unit/package-menus.unit.test.ts:17-23
  // [VSIX-PAIR-COMPARE] The retired implicit-compare commands. A single tree
  // row or hover can never name both endpoints of a pair, so these must stay
  // gone from every contribution surface.
  const IMPLICIT_COMPARE_COMMANDS = [
    "deslop.compareWithCanonical",
    "deslop.compareOccurrenceWithCanonical",
  ] as const;

# standing rules this breaks
AGENTS.md "Spec ids must be cross referenced across tests, code specs and plans ALWAYS"
AGENTS.md "Code, specs, and tests MUST agree. Where they don't, STOP and report."
AGENTS.md "Code and tests carry the ID in a comment so `grep [PARSE-` finds
           spec -> code -> tests."

# scope
affected surfaces: repo | cli | vsix | lsp | mcp
related issues: #524 (the [VSIX-PAIR-COMPARE] instance), #521, #522
```

### Acceptance Criteria (for AI)

- Every bracketed rule identifier cited anywhere in `clients/vscode/src`, `crates/*/src` or `crates/*/tests` resolves to a section in `docs/`; a check asserts the orphan count is zero.
- That check runs as part of the lint gate, so a newly invented identifier cannot merge without its written rule.
- Each of the thirty-six listed identifiers is either given a written section carrying that identifier, or renamed to the existing identifier it meant, or removed together with the code and tests that cite it — with no test left enforcing a rule that no document states.
- `[VSIX-PAIR-COMPARE]` specifically has a written section stating the comparison rules, and it agrees with whatever is decided in #524.
- `[RANK-SCORE]` resolves to a written section, since the contributor instructions use it as the worked example of a traceable identifier.
- Searching any one identifier returns its document, its code and its tests; asserted for at least three of the previously orphaned identifiers.

### Screenshots

title: Compare takes four clicks, cannot target the canonical occurrence, and cites a spec rule that does not exist
body:
### TL;DR

Comparing two occurrences now takes four clicks through a clumsy two-step selection flow, and the one comparison people actually want — this occurrence against the canonical one — was removed entirely. The panel displays which occurrence is canonical right at the top, but there is no way to compare anything against it.

### Details

The cluster panel puts a "Select for comparison" button on every single row, plus a separate "Compare selected occurrences" button above the list that stays greyed out until two rows have been picked. To see one difference a user has to find a row, click its button, scroll to another row, click its button, then scroll back up and click compare. Every row carries a button that does nothing on its own, so the list is twice as wide and twice as noisy as it needs to be, and the primary action is disabled almost all of the time.

That is not how selecting two things should work. Tapping the rows themselves should select them. A row is already the thing being pointed at; it does not need its own button to say so. Two rows tapped, comparison shown — no third button, no disabled state to stare at.

Worse, the comparison people want most is gone. The panel header already names the canonical occurrence — it is printed at the top of the panel next to the size and count. The obvious action is "show me how this one differs from the canonical one", a single tap on a single row. That used to exist and was deliberately removed, and there is now a test that actively keeps it removed. So the panel tells the user which occurrence is the reference and then refuses to compare anything to it.

There is also nothing that lets a user confirm a finding is genuinely identical. If two occurrences really are copies, the only difference between them should be leading whitespace, and seeing that at a glance is the fastest possible proof that the finding is real. Right now nothing shows that. Given that findings are currently being reported as duplicates when they are nothing of the sort, being able to see "these differ only by indentation" is the check that would catch it immediately.

Finally, the rule these decisions were made under does not exist. The code and its tests repeatedly cite a written rule for this behaviour, in more than ten places, but no such section exists in any of the specification documents. The behaviour is being enforced by tests against a rule nobody can read.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Open the repository in VS Code with the Deslop extension installed and let it analyse the workspace.
2. Open any finding from the Top Offenders list so the cluster panel appears.
3. Note the canonical occurrence named in the top-right of the panel.
4. Try to compare any occurrence against that canonical one — there is no control that does it.
5. Note that every row carries its own "Select for comparison" button, and that the "Compare selected occurrences" button above the list is greyed out.
6. Click "Select for comparison" on one row, then on a second row, then click "Compare selected occurrences" — four clicks to see one difference.
7. Click directly on a row instead of on its button and note that nothing is selected.
8. Open a finding whose occurrences are genuinely identical and note there is nothing showing that the only difference is indentation.

### Details (for AI)

```shell
# environment
deslop --version: 0.0.0-dev (workspace build, commit 77b4681b)
os: macOS 26.6.2
surface: vsix

# origin
1ecfc997  "Render no pair-only evidence on cluster surfaces; admission signals are
           pair-scoped; weight becomes mass (#485)"  merged Wed 2 Sep 2026
This one commit introduced the two-step select flow AND retired the canonical
compare commands. Confirmed with:
  git log -S "compareWithCanonical" --all -- clients/vscode/   -> 1ecfc997, d9f06d0c

# evidence - the retired commands, now test-enforced as gone
clients/vscode/src/test/unit/package-menus.unit.test.ts:17-23
  // [VSIX-PAIR-COMPARE] The retired implicit-compare commands. A single tree
  // row or hover can never name both endpoints of a pair, so these must stay
  // gone from every contribution surface.
  const IMPLICIT_COMPARE_COMMANDS = [
    "deslop.compareWithCanonical",
    "deslop.compareOccurrenceWithCanonical",
  ] as const;

# evidence - the refusal is written into the component
clients/vscode/webview-ui/src/cluster/OccurrenceList.tsx:24-25
  // [VSIX-PAIR-COMPARE] Pair evidence renders only after the user selects two
  // explicit endpoints; nothing here compares against an implicit canonical.
OccurrenceList.tsx:27  SELECT_FOR_COMPARISON = "Select for comparison"   # per-row button
OccurrenceList.tsx:28  COMPARE_SELECTED = "Compare selected occurrences" # gated button
OccurrenceList.tsx:139-146  per-row button -> pickCompareEndpoint(endpointOf(occurrence))
OccurrenceList.tsx:155-178  CompareSelectedButton, disabled unless left && right
Row click (OccurrenceList.tsx:80-88, 130-136) is wired to openOccurrence only, so
tapping a row cannot select it.

# evidence - the cited rule does not exist
grep -rn "VSIX-PAIR-COMPARE" docs/    -> no matches
grep -rn "VSIX-PAIR-COMPARE" clients/ -> 10+ matches across src and tests
The panel already renders the canonical occurrence in its header
(clients/vscode/webview-ui/src/cluster/main.tsx), so canonical is a first-class
concept on this exact surface while being unreachable as a compare target.

# related issues
#521  the same commit swapped what the row colours mean
#522  the contradictory colour tables the same commit left behind
#523  the same commit's field rename killed the agent tools
#520  a live finding whose 18 occurrences are not duplicates at all

# scope
affected surfaces: vsix
```

### Acceptance Criteria (for AI)

- A single tap on one occurrence row opens its comparison against the cluster's canonical occurrence; asserted end-to-end with one click and the resulting diff's two endpoints named.
- Tapping two occurrence rows selects both and opens their comparison; no per-row "Select for comparison" button exists on any row, asserted by the absence of that label anywhere in the rendered panel.
- No separate always-visible "Compare selected occurrences" button remains in the panel; asserted by the absence of that label in the rendered output.
- A comparison of two byte-identical occurrences renders a visible indication that the only difference is leading whitespace; asserted on a fixture whose two occurrences differ solely by indentation.
- A comparison of two occurrences that are not identical renders their real differences and does not claim a whitespace-only difference; asserted on the `js-cluster-extent-statement-runs` fixture from #520.
- A specification section defining the compare behaviour exists, carries the spec id every code and test comment cites, and states the canonical-compare and two-row-tap rules; `grep` for that id finds spec, code and tests.
- The retired command names are either restored with the canonical-compare behaviour or the test enforcing their absence is updated to match the new rule; no test enforces a rule that no specification states.

### Screenshots

pending — user has a cluster panel screenshot showing the canonical occurrence in the header, a per-row "Select for comparison" button on every row, and the greyed-out "Compare selected occurrences" button.

title: Every agent-facing Deslop tool fails with an opaque parse error when the report schema moves
body:
### TL;DR

Every Deslop tool an AI agent can call is dead. All of them fail with the same short message about a missing field. The agent gets no result at all, no hint about what is wrong, and no way to fix it — the only advice the error gives is nothing.

### Details

Deslop exposes a set of tools so an AI assistant can ask it questions — show me the worst duplicates, show me this one finding, show me what overlaps this file. The project's own instructions tell agents to use those tools first and fall back to the command line only if they are unavailable. Right now every single one of them fails immediately with `ipc transport failure: ipc report parse: missing field 'weight'`, and nothing comes back.

The cause is a version mismatch. A recent change renamed one field in the saved report from "weight" to "mass". The tool server that agents talk to was built before that rename, so it reads a report written by the newer code, looks for a field that no longer exists, and gives up. The two halves are simply from different days — the installed tool server is dated 31 August and the rename landed on 2 September.

The mismatch itself is ordinary and will happen again. What makes this a defect is the way it fails. The tool server does not check whether the report it is about to read was written by a compatible version, even though the report states its version right at the top. Instead it attempts to parse it and surfaces a raw internal parsing error. To anyone using it — human or agent — that message is unactionable: it does not say which two things disagree, does not say the installed extension is out of date, and does not suggest re-analysing or upgrading. An agent hitting this has no way to recover and, worse, may quietly fall back to guessing rather than measuring, which is exactly the failure mode the project is trying to eliminate.

The command line is unaffected and works correctly, so this is contained to the agent-facing tools. But those tools are the surface the instructions tell agents to prefer.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Install the packaged extension so its bundled tool server is on disk.
2. Configure the agent tool server to point at the bundled binary, using the absolute path form the project documentation specifies.
3. Run a full analysis with a newer build of the command-line tool so the saved report is written by the newer code.
4. From the agent, call any Deslop tool — for example the one that lists the worst offenders, or the one that fetches a single finding by its id.
5. Observe that every call returns `ipc transport failure: ipc report parse: missing field 'weight'` and no result.

### Details (for AI)

```shell
# environment
deslop --version: 0.0.0-dev (workspace build, commit 77b4681b)
os: macOS 26.6.2
surface: mcp
vsix version: nimblesite.deslop-live-0.0.0-dev (also installed: 0.32.0, 0.33.0 darwin-arm64)

# invocation
configured server (from ~/.claude.json):
  command: /Users/christianfindlay/.vscode/extensions/nimblesite.deslop-live-0.0.0-dev/bin/darwin-arm64/deslop-mcp
  args: ["--root", "."]
this is the absolute-VSIX-path form AGENTS.md mandates for external MCP clients.

# evidence
mcp__deslop__cluster-by-id  { id: "9a38a61" }
  -> ipc transport failure: ipc cluster parse: missing field `weight`
mcp__deslop__top-offenders  { n: 1, max_occurrences: 3 }
  -> ipc transport failure: ipc report parse: missing field `weight`
every other deslop tool fails identically; no tool returns a result.

# cause
1ecfc997 (PR #485, merged Wed 2 Sep 2026) renamed ReportCluster.weight: Float
  -> ReportCluster.mass: Int on the live IPC wire.
bundled binaries predate it:
  ls -la ~/.vscode/extensions/nimblesite.deslop-live-0.0.0-dev/bin/darwin-arm64/
    deslop      29952160  Aug 31 14:37
    deslop-mcp  27268848  Aug 31 14:37
report the server reads was written by post-rename code:
  .deslop/deslop-report.json  tool_version "0.0.0-dev"
  cluster keys: id, rank, rank_band, mass, canonical_node_count, occurrences, ...
  (no `weight` key present)
workspace source is already clean:
  grep -rn "weight" crates/deslop-mcp/src   -> no matches

# the defect
The server parses the report without first comparing its `tool_version` against
its own, despite `tool_version` being the first field of the document. A schema
disagreement therefore surfaces as a raw serde field error rather than a named,
actionable condition. There is no version guard, no re-analysis path, and no
message naming the two disagreeing versions.

# scope
affected surfaces: mcp
unaffected: cli (verified working on the same report)
related issues: #520, #521, #522
```

### Acceptance Criteria (for AI)

- The tool server compares the report's `tool_version` against its own before parsing, and a mismatch produces a named error condition rather than a serde field error.
- The mismatch message names both versions, the report path, and the remedy (re-analyse, or update the extension); a test asserts each of those four elements is present in the message.
- A test drives a tool call against a report written in the pre-rename schema and asserts the exact user-facing message, so an opaque parse error can never reach a caller again.
- After a version mismatch is detected, the server either re-analyses and returns a correct result, or fails with the named condition; it never returns a partial or empty result that a caller could mistake for "no duplicates found".
- `mcp__deslop__top-offenders` and `mcp__deslop__cluster-by-id` both return results against a report written by the current engine; asserted on a fixture with a known cluster id and occurrence count.
- The packaged extension cannot ship a tool server and an engine whose wire schemas disagree; a build or release gate asserts both binaries in one bundle share a wire-schema version.

### Screenshots

None.

title: Three contradictory severity colour tables, and design.ts comments call the shipped one a defect
body:
### TL;DR

The extension now holds three different sets of rules for what colour a finding gets, they disagree with each other, and the comments sitting right next to them in the file say the one actually being used is a known bug. The Top Offenders list also paints from a completely different palette than the pop-up card and the in-editor highlighting, so the same finding can be one colour in the list and another colour in the editor.

### Details

One file in the extension defines two colour tables one after the other. The first is keyed by how big a finding is. The comment directly above it says, in the file today, that this table "is NOT the paint", and that using it to colour an editor surface "is what made rank-1 shape-only scaffolding crimson" — in other words, using it is precisely the bug that turns a weakly-matched top finding bright red. The second table is keyed by how strong the evidence is, and its comment says colour is a function of the evidence alone, so a finding is "coloured by what kind of duplicate it is and never by where it happens to sort".

Both of those statements are now false in the shipped product. The pop-up card and the in-editor highlighting do read the second table, but the value they look up is computed from the finding's size ranking and then renamed — biggest becomes "error", next biggest becomes "warning". So the table named for evidence is being handed position and told it is evidence. Meanwhile the Top Offenders list uses neither table: it has a third, private one that maps size ranking straight onto the editor's own red, orange, blue and grey chart colours.

That third table is why the list and the editor can disagree with each other. Every other surface paints from Deslop's own palette; the list paints from VS Code's chart palette. Those are different colours for the same finding, in the same product, at the same moment — and consistency across panels is supposed to be non-negotiable.

The practical result is that nobody can say what a colour means, because three different answers are live at once and the file's own comments describe a fourth arrangement that no longer exists. This is the machinery underneath the colour-meaning issue: that one asks what the colours should mean, this one is about the fact that the code currently holds several contradictory answers and a comment calling the shipped one a defect.

For completeness, and deliberately not part of this issue: the webview holds a fourth copy of the size-keyed table. That one is a documented mirror with a parity check in the pipeline, because the webview cannot import extension-host code.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Open `clients/vscode/src/design.ts` and read lines 28 to 49 — two colour tables whose comments contradict what the product does.

4. Open `clients/vscode/src/severity.ts` at line 30 and see that the value fed to the evidence-keyed table is derived from the finding's size ranking.
5. In VS Code, compare a finding's dot colour in the Top Offenders list against the same finding's pop-up card and in-editor highlight colour.

```shell
                             clients/vscode/src/decorations/manager.ts:99
   fed by clusterSeverity(), which resolves rank_band via
   clients/vscode/src/severity.ts:30  { worst: "error", top10: "warning", ... }
   => the evidence-keyed table receives a position-derived level, so its comment

2. SEVERITY_STYLE         <- clients/vscode/src/tree/nodes.ts:44-49
```

title: Restore evidence-driven cluster colour: red no longer means identical, amber no longer means nearly identical
body:
### TL;DR

Red used to mean "these are identical" and brown/orange used to mean "these are nearly identical". One pull request swapped what the colours are keyed to — red now just means "one of the biggest findings" and brown means "one of the next biggest" — while keeping the exact same colours and the exact same icons. Nothing on screen changed, so there was no visible sign that the meaning had been replaced.

### Details

In the Top Offenders list the top 16 rows are red and the rows below them are brown. That split is purely by size ranking now. It has nothing to do with whether the code actually matches. A finding with no evidence at all that its members are copies can be painted the loudest red, and a finding that genuinely is character-for-character identical can be painted a quieter colour simply because it is smaller.

This is the worst kind of regression because it is invisible. The change kept red as red, kept brown as brown, and kept the same filled-circle and large-circle icons. Only the thing being looked up changed: it used to be how well the code matched, and now it is where the finding sorts by size. A user reading the panel has no way to know the vocabulary was swapped underneath them — the picture is identical and the meaning is not.

The project already knew this was wrong before it happened. The written rules at the time said red is reserved for identical code, "the only group whose evidence is character-by-character proof", and they carried an explicit warning that the panel had once been coloured by size ranking and that doing so was "a defect, not a staging decision". The warning even described the exact failure: a weakly-matched finding ranks first and comes out crimson while a genuinely identical one just below it comes out blue — the colours land inverted. There was a test holding that line. The same pull request deleted the test, rewrote the rules to say colour follows size ranking, and shipped the behaviour the old rules had called a defect.

That predicted failure is now live and is filed separately: the rank-1 red finding on the website's test folder contains 18 pieces of code that are all different from one another, in three different lengths. Fixing that one finding does not fix this, because every future weakly-matched finding will still be painted red — the colour rule itself no longer looks at the evidence.

One decision has to be made before any code is touched. The report currently carries no match-strength label on a finding at all; the same pull request made those labels apply only to an explicitly compared pair of snippets, and the current written rules state they are forbidden on findings. So restoring "red means identical" is not a palette edit — it needs a decision about what evidence a finding is allowed to carry. That decision is the substance of this issue.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Open the repository in VS Code with the Deslop extension installed and let it analyse the workspace.
2. Open the Top Offenders panel.
3. Observe that rows ranked 1 through 16 are red and rows from 17 down are brown.
4. Expand the red row at rank 1 and open its listed occurrences — they are not identical to each other.
5. Expand a brown row further down whose occurrences are character-for-character identical, and note it is painted more quietly than the red row above it that is not identical at all.
6. Run `git show 1ecfc997 -- clients/vscode/src/tree/nodes.ts` and read the removed and added colour tables.
7. Run `git show 1ecfc997^:docs/specs/severity.md` to read the previous written rules, which state the opposite of today's.

### Details (for AI)

```shell

deslop --version: 0.0.0-dev (workspace build, commit 77b4681b)
os: macOS 26.6.2
surface: vsix | lsp
vsix version: current workspace build

# the commit that changed it
1ecfc997  "Render no pair-only evidence on cluster surfaces; admission signals are
           pair-scoped; weight becomes mass (#485)"
author: Christian Findlay, Wed 2 Sep 2026, merged via PR #485

# evidence - the swap, colours and icons preserved
git show 1ecfc997 -- clients/vscode/src/tree/nodes.ts
  -  identical:        { icon: "circle-filled",       color: "charts.red" },
  -  nearly_identical: { icon: "circle-large-filled", color: "charts.orange" },
  -  structural_only:  { icon: "circle-slash",        color: "charts.foreground" },
  -  loosely_similar:  { icon: "circle-outline",      color: "charts.blue" },
  -  same_behavior:    { icon: "sparkle",             color: "charts.purple" },
  +  worst:  { icon: "circle-filled",       color: "charts.red" },
  +  top10:  { icon: "circle-large-filled", color: "charts.orange" },
  +  mid:    { icon: "circle-outline",      color: "charts.blue" },
  +  faint:  { icon: "circle-outline",      color: "charts.grey" },
Same red, same orange, same circle-filled / circle-large-filled icons. Only the
key changed: clone classification -> mass rank band. The UI is visually identical
before and after, so the meaning change shipped with no visible signal.

# evidence - assertions deleted in the same commit
git show --numstat 1ecfc997
  57  157  clients/vscode/src/test/unit/severity.unit.test.ts   # net -100 lines
  38   50  clients/vscode/src/severity.ts
  34   76  docs/specs/severity.md
deleted assertion (pre-485):
  "a demoted shape-only family is not painted with act-now severity"
replacement assertion (current severity.unit.test.ts:94):
  "no surface may derive severity from a clone kind"            # the inverse contract

# evidence - the rules before and after
git show 1ecfc997^:docs/specs/severity.md   [SEVERITY-DESLOP-MAP]
  | Identical        | error       | red   |
  | NearlyIdentical  | warning     | amber |
  | LooselySimilar   | information | blue  |
  | StructuralOnly   | hint        | muted |
  | SameBehavior     | hint        | grey  |
  "`error` is reserved for `Identical`, the only bucket whose evidence is byte proof."
  "The VSIX previously coloured by rank percentile, and that was a defect, not a
   staging decision. ... the paint came out *inverted*: the demoted family rendered
   crimson -- the 'safe to extract' colour -- while the byte-proven `Identical`
   clone one rank below it rendered blue."
current docs/specs/severity.md  [SEVERITY-COLOR]
  "A cluster's colour cannot imply that it is identical, near-identical,
   structural-only, semantic, or content-proven."

# current code
clients/vscode/src/tree/nodes.ts:44-49   SEVERITY_STYLE keyed by rank_band
clients/vscode/src/severity.ts:30        { worst: "error", top10: "warning", ... }

# design tension to resolve first
PR #485 removed `bucket` from `ReportCluster` on the live IPC wire; docs/specs/SPEC.md:128
records pair classifications as "pair-only ... forbidden on clusters". Restoring
evidence-driven colour requires deciding what match-strength evidence a cluster may
carry. Options: (a) re-admit a cluster-level classification derived from the elected
pair; (b) colour from the elected pair's classification without storing it on the
cluster; (c) keep rank colour but add a separate evidence channel to the row.

# related issues
#520  the live instance -- rank-1 red finding whose 18 occurrences are all different
#522  the contradictory colour tables left behind in the client

# related spec sections
[SEVERITY-COLOR] [SEVERITY-MODEL] [SEVERITY-DESLOP-MAP] [SEVERITY-BAND]  docs/specs/severity.md
[CLONE-BUCKETS]                                                          docs/specs/taxonomy.md
[FUSED-PAIR-SIGNALS] [FUSED-SCOPE]                                       docs/specs/fused.md
```

### Acceptance Criteria (for AI)

- A cluster whose occurrences are byte-identical is painted red, asserted on a fixture where that family does **not** rank first, so the assertion cannot pass by ranking accident.
- A cluster whose occurrences are not byte-identical is never painted red, asserted on a fixture whose rank-1 cluster is weakly matched — the exact inversion case the pre-485 spec described.
- A byte-identical cluster ranked below a weakly-matched cluster is painted a stronger colour than the cluster above it; one assertion block covers both rows' colours and both rank positions.
- Brown/orange is asserted to mean nearly-identical on a fixture holding a renamed-identifier clone family, distinguished in the same test from both the red byte-identical family and an uncoloured weak family.
- The assertion deleted by PR #485 is restored in substance, and the assertion count in `clients/vscode/src/test/unit/severity.unit.test.ts` is greater than or equal to the pre-485 count of that file.
- `docs/specs/severity.md`, `clients/vscode/src/severity.ts`, `clients/vscode/src/tree/nodes.ts` and `clients/vscode/src/test/unit/severity.unit.test.ts` all state the same colour rule; a spec-check run reports no disagreement between them.
- A test asserts that changing what a colour is keyed to cannot ship without changing the colour or icon tokens themselves, so a future silent swap of meaning fails the suite.

title: Rank-1 red cluster groups 18 unrelated Playwright statements of 2, 3 and 5 lines as one duplicate
body:
### TL;DR

Deslop's top-ranked finding on the website's test folder is not duplicated code at all. It groups 18 completely different lines of test code into one duplicate, and they are not even the same length: 11 are 2 lines long, 6 are 3 lines, and 1 is 5 lines. This single wrong finding accounts for a quarter of all the duplication the report claims for that folder.

### Details

Running Deslop over the website's test folder produces 30 findings. The one it puts at the very top — the biggest, red-flagged finding a user sees first — claims 18 snippets are copies of each other. They are ordinary browser-test lines with nothing in common. One clicks a menu and types into a search box. Another checks that a sidebar has four sections. Another checks two Chinese-language links. Another checks a heading and a card count. No two of them are the same text.

The clearest proof that this cannot be right is that the members are different sizes. A duplicate is supposed to be the same chunk of code appearing in several places, so every member should be about the same size. Here they range from 2 lines to 5 lines, and from 117 to 238 characters — one member is twice the size of another. The report at the same time claims all 18 share one common shape of 31 elements, which cannot be true of a 2-line snippet and a 5-line snippet simultaneously.

The damage is not cosmetic. This finding is scored 527 out of 2148 for the whole scan, so a quarter of everything the report calls duplicated is this one wrong answer. It also pushes the headline number for the folder to "21.9% duplicated". Because it ranks first it is painted the loudest red, so the most alarming thing Deslop says about this code is entirely wrong. Nothing suppressed it — the report says nothing was hidden, so no false-positive filter fired.

On the red colour specifically: red currently means "one of the biggest findings", not "identical", and the extension follows the written rules correctly on that point. The defect here is not the colour — it is that this finding should not exist at all, let alone rank first. What the colours ought to mean is tracked separately.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Clone the repository and build the CLI with `make ci`.
2. Run `./target/release/deslop site/tests --embeddings off --no-incremental --output /tmp/deslop-sitetests --nohtml`.
3. Open `/tmp/deslop-sitetests.txt`.
4. Look at the first entry, which reports 18 occurrences.
5. Open each of the 18 listed file and line locations and compare them — they are 18 different pieces of code.
6. Compare the line ranges in that same list: one runs 29 to 30 (2 lines), one runs 48 to 50 (3 lines), and one runs 490 to 494 (5 lines).

### Acceptance Criteria (for AI)

- `crates/deslop/tests/cluster_extent_statement_runs.rs::unrelated_statement_runs_are_never_published_as_one_duplication` passes at every threshold it drives (12, 30, 45) without any assertion being weakened or removed.
- No reported cluster contains two occurrences whose line spans differ; asserted across every cluster in the fixture report, not just the top one.
- No reported cluster groups `site/tests/issues-publication.spec.js:48:50`, `site/tests/issues.spec.js:29:30` and `site/tests/issues.spec.js:490:494` together; asserted on the exact paths and line numbers.
- No multi-line occurrence begins part-way along its opening line; asserted with the offending line text in the failure message.
- The two fixture files in `crates/deslop/tests/fixtures/js-cluster-extent-statement-runs/` produce a repository duplication percentage of exactly 0.0, and no cluster spans both files.
- `canonical_node_count` agrees with every occurrence in the cluster: no cluster claims an element count that no member's span can hold.
- Re-running the `site/tests` scan reports a headline percentage below 21.9%, and the new value is asserted exactly rather than as an inequality alone.

title: Python test-dict-literal filter hides a duplicated test whose asserts compare against computed calls
body:
## Defect

`cluster_filters::python::is_test_dict_literal_cluster` convicts a cluster whenever every member sits inside a `test_*` function, the reported range encloses exactly one dictionary literal, and the members' top-level key sets differ. It never looks at what else the range holds. When the assertions beside the dictionary compare against **computed** calls, the two functions are one test written twice and the cluster is a real duplicate, but the filter hides it — a false negative.

The committed fixture `crates/deslop/tests/fixtures/python-dict-assert-rhs-logic` only escapes this because each file opens with a module docstring, so the reported view is the whole file (`[PIPELINE-FINGERPRINT-MERKLE-ROOT]`) and `enclosing_kind(.., "function_definition")` finds no function enclosing a range that starts above the function. The same two files with the docstrings removed are hidden.

## Reproduction

Copy the two fixture files, delete the first three lines of each (the docstring and blank lines), then:

```
deslop <dir> --output <out>/report --no-incremental --min-nodes 12 --embeddings off
```

Result: `clusters_hidden: 1`, no visible cluster. Change `"window"` to `"period"` in `test_statement_window.py` so the key sets match and the pair is reported at `L1-8` in both files. The only difference between the two runs is the dictionary key, which is exactly what the filter keys on.

Reproduced on `main` (f92300e5) and on `corpus` (49e026c1).

## Expected

A `test_*` function whose assertions compare chained-subscript reads against a call (`== reconcile_amount(...)`) carries logic no payload table proves; the dictionary-key difference alone must not convict it. `python_dict_assert::is_chained_dict_assert_snippet` already refuses a computed right operand (`comparison_against_literal`); `is_test_dict_literal_cluster` needs the same proof before it can treat the range as data.

## Spec

`[CLONE-NOISE-*]` for the Python test-payload filters; the fixture's intent is documented in `crates/deslop/tests/python_dict_assert_rhs_logic.rs`.

title: Collect-then-assert_eq test idiom is ranked a worst-band duplicate across nine unrelated tests
body:
## TL;DR

Deslop reports the ordinary "collect a list, then assert it equals the expected list" test pattern as one of the worst duplicates in its own repository. Nine unrelated tests are grouped as copies of each other because they all build a list and compare it, even though each one collects something different.

## Details

Running Deslop on its own workspace puts a cluster of nine test snippets in the worst band. Every snippet is two statements: build a list from a collection, then assert that list equals an expected list. That is the normal way to check a list in a Rust test. The nine tests collect completely different things: file paths, byte lengths, cluster ids, ranking bands, member indexes and argument names. No developer would pull these into a shared helper, and nothing about them is a copy.

Deslop already has a rule that ignores the "iterate, map a field, collect" idiom, but it only fires when every snippet maps a plain field-then-method call. Here the mapping expressions vary (subtraction, a lookup helper, a clone, a last-element pick), so the rule stands down and the group is reported at full strength. The result is a top-ranked finding that nobody can act on, which pushes real duplicates further down the list.

## Steps To Reproduce

1. Clone https://github.com/nimblesite/deslop and check out branch `corpus`.
2. Run `deslop . --output /tmp/deslop --min-nodes 30 --nohtml --notext`.
3. Open `/tmp/deslop.json` and find the cluster with id `73ca82580ef73693`.
4. See that it sits in the `worst` rank band with nine occurrences across `crates/deslop/tests` and `crates/deslop-core/tests`.
5. Open any two of the occurrences and see that they collect different things and compare against different expected lists.

## Details (for AI)

```shell
# environment
deslop --version: 0.0.0-dev
os: macOS 26 (Darwin 25.5.0)
surface: cli | mcp
vsix version: n/a

# context
command: deslop . --output /tmp/deslop --min-nodes 30 --nohtml --notext
mcp: top-offenders n=10 on the Deslop workspace, generation 27

# evidence
cluster id: 73ca82580ef73693
occurrence count: 9
bucket: nearly_identical
rank band: worst (rank 2 after the dedup pass on the corpus branch)
canonical_node_count: 43
signals: shape=1.00 structural=1.00 token_jaccard=1.00 pair_agreement=0.79 pair_rename_consistency=0.00 literal_fraction=0.00 embedding_cos=0.00
files involved:
  - crates/deslop/tests/cross_cluster_collapse.rs:211 (paths -> Vec<&str>)
  - crates/deslop/tests/cross_cluster_collapse.rs:221 (spans -> Vec<u64>, saturating_sub)
  - crates/deslop/tests/cross_cluster_collapse.rs:391 (spans -> Vec<u64>)
  - crates/deslop/tests/metrics_folder_rollup.rs:144 (folder paths)
  - crates/deslop/tests/report_golden/contract.rs:285 (rank_band via a field() helper)
  - crates/deslop-core/tests/live.rs:130 (cluster ids)
  - crates/deslop-core/tests/pair_admission_bounded_max.rs:86 (Option::map + unwrap_or_default, members)
  - crates/deslop-core/tests/refactor_merge.rs:360 (filter_map + last(), then ensure!)
  - crates/deslop-core/tests/report_fixture_file_identity.rs:53 (filter_map paths)
shape of every member:
  let <name>: Vec<T> = <collection>.iter().map(<closure>).collect();
  assert_eq!(<name>, vec![<literals>], "<message>");
existing filter: [CLONE-NOISE-RUST-ITER-COLLECT] crates/deslop-core/src/cluster_filters/rust.rs is_rust_iter_collect_idiom_cluster / snippet_contains_iter_collect_idiom
  requires every member to contain .iter().map(|x| x.field.method()).collect(); the closures above do not all have that shape, so the filter stands down
```

## Acceptance Criteria (for AI)

- A fixture repository with two Rust test files, each holding one `let names: Vec<_> = items.iter().map(<different closure>).collect(); assert_eq!(names, vec![<different literals>], "<different message>");` block, produces no cluster over those blocks, asserted on the rendered JSON report (zero clusters whose occurrences cover both blocks).
- The same fixture with the two blocks made byte-identical (same closure, same literals, same message) still produces exactly one `identical` cluster with occurrence count 2 covering both files, so verbatim copies of an assertion block stay visible.
- On the Deslop workspace itself, no cluster whose every member is the collect-then-assert_eq shape above appears in the `worst` or `top10` rank bands.
- The test that pins this lives beside the other [CLONE-NOISE-RUST-*] filter tests and asserts the cluster id list, occurrence counts, file paths and bucket on the rendered report, not on internals.

title: Same-file bucket completion is quadratic in bucket size on generated files
body:
## What

[FUSED-CANDIDATE-BUCKET-STAR] now pairs every two members of a structural-hash bucket that share a file, because inside one file the star's canonical is an accident of write order and a differing sibling ahead of a byte-identical copy deleted that copy from the report entirely (`same_file_rescue::a_shape_sibling_may_not_hide_an_exact_same_file_copy`).

All-pairs is complete, but it is quadratic in the number of same-file members of one bucket, and a file's Merkle buckets are per-window-level, so the factor multiplies.

## Measured

One synthetic C# file, `n` structurally identical methods, `--min-nodes 12`:

| n | wall | retained pairs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 100 | 0.22 s | — |
| 200 | 0.87 s | — |
| 400 | 3.83 s | 718,998 |
| 800 | 19.49 s | — |

At n=400 the cost is 3,452 ms of 3,830 ms in `pair_content_gate`, measuring 718k candidate edges from one 2,800-line file, at 130 MiB RSS.

Real code is far cheaper: this repository (7,180 files) went 3.0 s -> 3.7 s, 52,398 retained pairs, 424 MiB. The pathological shape is machine-generated code — protobuf/OpenAPI clients, freezed output — where one file holds hundreds of identically shaped declarations.

## Why it is not simply bounded

A cap on bucket size is a count standing in for a structural question, which `[CLONE-NOISE]` and `declaration_family.rs` both forbid. Pairing only adjacent members restores the order dependence the change exists to remove. Grouping members by content-key sequence is complete and collapses byte-identical members, but a data table has all-distinct rows and stays quadratic.

The bound that would work is a MinHash over **raw content keys** rather than normalised k-grams: the content gate's `agreement` is a metric-like quantity over those keys, so an LSH pass over them would supply candidate neighbours in near-linear time and the bucket completion could ask it instead of enumerating. That is a new pass, not a tweak.

## Acceptance

- A file holding several hundred identically shaped declarations does not multiply the retained pair population by the square of its member count.
- `same_file_rescue::a_shape_sibling_may_not_hide_an_exact_same_file_copy` and `dart_forwarding_fail_open::wrappers_sharing_a_body_keep_the_family_visible` stay green: recall still does not depend on write order.

title: Cross-file occurrence extents disagree: one file's widest sibling window wins alone, padding a cluster with a package prologue and an unmatched type declaration
body:
## What happens

`collapse_overlapping_per_file` elects one representative **per file, independently of every other file**, preferring the widest byte range. When one file happens to hold a wider overlapping sibling window than its counterpart, that file publishes the wide window and the other publishes the correct authored declaration. The cluster then claims two regions are copies of one another when one of them carries a package clause, an import block and a type declaration the other has no counterpart for.

`crates/deslop/tests/cluster_extent_alignment.rs` already documents this mechanism in its module doc. The Python fixture case is fixed; the Go case below is not.

## Reproduction

Fixture `crates/deslop/tests/fixtures/go-cluster-extent-alignment` — two Go files sharing exactly one authored pair of tree-writing functions:

```
cluster nodes=235 mass=235
   json_report.go:1-55  (1333 bytes)   <- starts at `package report`
   text_report.go:38-71 (1022 bytes)   <- starts at `func GenTextTree`
```

`json_report.go` lines 1–21 are the package clause, an import block carrying three imports `text_report.go` does not have, and `type settingSpec struct` — none of which appear in the other occurrence. Reproduces at `--min-nodes` 8, 12, 20 and 30 alike.

## Impact on reported figures

`duplicated_loc` projects these line sets ([METRICS-REPO]), so the padding lands directly in the headline percentage. On the fixture: `duplicated_loc = 103` of `analysed_loc = 126` → **81.7 %** for two files that share 34 lines.

Confirmed in the wild on cobra v1.9.1 (`40b5bc1437a564fc795d388b23835e84f54cd1d1`), cluster `2fbda1bba17a8450`:

```
doc/md_docs.go:125-158   1053 bytes
doc/rest_docs.go:138-170 1004 bytes
doc/yaml_docs.go:30-85   1953 bytes   <- 981 bytes too early
```

The duplicated region in `yaml_docs.go` truly starts at byte 1735 (`func GenYamlTree(`), giving a 972-byte span consistent with the other two. The reported `start_byte` is 754, swallowing `type cmdOption struct` and `type cmdDoc struct` (lines 30–52). The engine simultaneously publishes the correct alignment as two other clusters (`md_docs.go:125-129 ↔ yaml_docs.go:53-57` and `rest_docs.go:145-170 ↔ yaml_docs.go:60-85`), so `yaml_docs.go:53-85` is counted three times.

Scale across four scanned repositories (deslop `e8a215e99fb962b8ce2320dcf2fc092da9343332`), clusters whose occurrence byte extents differ by more than 1.5x:

| repo | ref | clusters | skewed | engine `duplicated_loc` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| click | 8.5.0 | 311 | 51 | 3930 |
| cobra | v1.9.1 | 455 | 56 | 7863 |
| axios | v1.9.0 | 156 | 10 | 3190 |
| Polly | v5.6.0 | 1637 | 186 | 45782 |

Some skew is legitimate Type-3 variation; the cobra case above is not.

## Failing test

`crates/deslop/tests/cluster_extent_alignment.rs::a_go_pair_is_not_padded_with_the_prologue_and_types_of_one_file`, sitting beside the Python case it extends. Currently red:

```
[PIPELINE-CLUSTER-EXACT-SCOPE] every occurrence must open the authored
declaration; only 1 of 2 do, so the cluster mixes a declaration window
with a whole-file window: spans=[(1, 55), (38, 71)]
```

## Where the defect is

`collapse_overlapping_single_file` in `crates/deslop-core/src/cluster.rs` picks the representative by authored scope then **widest byte range**, with no requirement that the winners across files describe the same view. The fix has to make the election cross-file aware; widening a per-file preference cannot do it.

title: Specs document a content_gate config table, [tuning] section and --tune flag that do not exist in code
body:
`docs/specs/exclusion.md` and `docs/specs/fused.md` describe a `content_gate` configuration table, a `[tuning]` config section and a `--tune <table>.<key>=<value>` CLI flag. None of them exist in the code.

Searched the whole tree (`crates/`, not just `deslop-core`):

- `content_gate` — zero occurrences in any `.rs` file. The two hits are prose in `crates/deslop/tests/common/verbatim_subgroup.rs`, which cites `content_gate.support_floor` in a doc comment.
- `--tune`, `[tuning]`, `struct Tuning` — zero occurrences.
- `structural_only_max_support` — zero occurrences outside `docs/specs/`.

What exists instead is two hardcoded constants in `crates/deslop-core/src/buckets.rs`:

```rust
pub const CONTENT_SUPPORT_FLOOR: f64 = 0.7;
pub const CONTENT_PROMOTE_FLOOR: f64 = 0.85;
```

Three separate problems fall out of that.

**The specs assert an invariant over a key that does not exist.** `exclusion.md` lists `content_gate.structural_only_max_support < content_gate.support_floor` among the cross-key invariants "rejected at load", and `fused.md`'s lever table gives it a value (0.05), a file, a line and a `**Defect.**` provenance verdict. There is no loader, no key, and no rejection. A reader auditing the gate is reading a description of software that was never written.

**The lever table's file:line references are stale.** `fused.md` cites `buckets.rs:237` for `support_floor` and `buckets.rs:215` for `structural_only_max_support`. `buckets.rs` is 15 lines long. The spec IDs are meant to make `grep` walk spec → code → tests; these coordinates walk nowhere.

**The thresholds are not configurable, which AGENTS.md requires.** "All threshold numbers are configurable — define the defaults as constants but allow the user to override these in the config." Both content-gate floors are compile-time constants with no override path, so a user cannot reproduce a scan at a different operating point, and the "Precedence, highest first: `--tune` CLI flag, then the editor settings channel in `crate::state`, then `[tuning]`, then the compiled default" paragraph in `exclusion.md` describes a precedence chain with exactly one live link.

Not introduced by any recent branch — the same text is on `main` and predates the [FUSED-CONTENT-GATE] floor work. Filing rather than fixing in place because closing it means either building the config surface the specs promise or deleting the promise, and that is a decision about the product, not a documentation touch-up.

Spec IDs: [FUSED-CONTENT-GATE], [CLONE-BUCKETS-ROUTING], [EXCLUSION-CONFIG].

title: Six tests fail on Windows because assertions compare forward-slash paths against rendered platform paths
body:
## What

Running the full suite on Windows fails six tests. Every one compares a forward-slash path against a report or refusal that carries the platform separator.

```
defaults::default_run_hides_intentional_test_fixture_corpora_from_dogfood_report
diff_ingest_refusals::copy_sections_that_disagree_with_the_tree_are_refused
diff_ingest_refusals::metadata_only_copy_counts_every_line_and_breaches_the_gate
diff_ingest_refusals::missing_supported_target_in_root_is_refused_as_stale
diff_scoped_ingest::diff_from_stdin_tags_identically
diff_scoped_reporting::diff_tags_the_four_populations_and_metrics_add_up
```

Two examples.

`defaults` asserts a visible cluster whose occurrence path contains `src/billing/`; the report renders `src\billing\InvoiceAlpha.cs`:

```
real source clones must remain visible after hiding fixture corpora
"path":"src\billing\InvoiceAlpha.cs"
```

`diff_ingest_refusals` asserts the refusal names `src/missing.rs`; it names `src\missing.rs`:

```
✘ failed: diff does not match the scanned tree: src\missing.rs differs at line 1;
  regenerate the diff against the analysed revision
```

The two `diff_scoped_*` failures are the same cause one step further on: diff ingest matches patch targets against the scanned tree, so on Windows the added files are not recognised and their cluster never reaches the report (`no cluster with paths ["src/fresh_a.rs", "src/fresh_b.rs"]`).

## Why CI is green

`make coverage-run`, which runs the whole suite, runs on `ubuntu-latest`. The `windows` job builds the binaries and runs only `cargo test --release -p deslop-mcp --test tcp_transport`. Nothing runs these six on Windows.

## Why it matters beyond the tests

The rendered path separator is part of the output contract on every surface — JSON, text, HTML, LSP and MCP. A consumer that matches paths from a Windows report against paths from a Linux one gets different strings for the same file, and [PIPELINE-DETERMINISM] is about corpus state rather than host. Deciding whether reports always render `/` is a specification question, not a test fix; the tests are asserting the answer they expect.

## Not from the subsumption work

Found while running the full suite locally on Windows during the ranked-build performance change. That change touches clustering and report materialisation, never path rendering, and the plain scan of the same fixture publishes all three clusters correctly.

title: Flutter StatelessWidget boilerplate ranks #2 on the Flutter corpus (1,349 occurrences, mass 40,440)
Whole-file views weld onto function clones through one-sided rescue pairs and widen the published extent
body:
## Symptom

`crates/deslop/tests/fixtures/js-mjs-cjs-family` (`--min-nodes 8`): 0.32.0 published the three `reconcileInventory` copies at function extent (lines 3–17 in each file). The current tip publishes whole files (1–17, 1–17, 1–19), so the differing `import` specifiers and the `module.exports` line of `stock.cjs` are counted as duplicated (53/53 LOC instead of 45/53).

## Cause

[FUSED-SHARED-SUBTREE-ECHO] refuses a rescue pair whose *both* endpoints enclose an exact whole-function clone, and (since 9645392) one whose both endpoints lie inside it. A pair with one endpoint enclosing the clone and the other a window inside the neighbouring copy is neither, so the whole-file view is rescued for free, welded into the function component, and wins the per-file election as the wider authored node ([PIPELINE-CLUSTER-EXACT-SCOPE]).

Refusing that one-sided case restores the function extents here, but it also changes three settled pins (`cross_cluster_collapse::wider_cross_file_view_survives_subsumption`, both `js_ts_extensions` byte-truth pins) whose expectations were written against the welded output, so it was not landed in 0.33.0.

## Status

Same three copies reported in both versions; the extent is wider than authored. Recorded in `docs/release-audit.md`.

title: embedding_route_invariance: embeddings on welds the byte-identical ledger_d/ledger_e whole-file pair into the ts-mixed-band near-miss family
body:
## Symptom

`embedding_route_invariance::embeddings_on_reports_every_file_set_embeddings_off_reported` fails on `ts-mixed-band` (`--min-nodes 12`).

With embeddings off the report publishes three views: the whole-file near-miss family `[ledger_a, ledger_c, ledger_d, ledger_e]`, the byte-identical tail window `[ledger_a, ledger_d, ledger_e]`, and the byte-identical whole-file pair `[ledger_d, ledger_e]`.

With embeddings on (mock Ollama) the `[ledger_d, ledger_e]` pair is welded into the wider family and no cluster names exactly that file set, so the test's invariant — a restored cosine may add findings but never remove one ([FUSED-PAIR-SIGNALS]) — is violated.

## Cause

The embeddings-on route admits pairs carrying a cosine above `candidates.embedding_support_floor` without the content guard and without the shared-subtree echo test ([FUSED-SHARED-SUBTREE-ECHO]), so cross-level pairs between the whole-file views and windows inside the neighbouring copies weld the exact pair into the near-miss component. The embeddings-off route refuses those pairs as echoes.

## Status

Embedding routes are a 0.33.0 non-goal. The test is ignored with this issue as its reason and stays in the curated skip set; its assertions are unchanged. Run it with `cargo test --release -p deslop --test suite -- --ignored embeddings_on_reports_every_file_set`.

title: Make pair/compare preserve shared-subtree rescue admission
body:
## TL;DR

`pair/compare` says a reported duplicate pair was rejected, even though that exact pair entered the report. The response contradicts the detector's decision and can mislead users and agents auditing a finding.

## Details

Deslop reports the F# pair as part of a duplicate cluster. Asking Deslop to compare those same two source ranges returns `admitted: false` and says the pair failed its guards.

The measured values support the report's decision. The comparison response is wrong because it treats the later detailed similarity measurement as if it had been available during the earlier candidate check, then rejects the pair through a different path.

## Steps To Reproduce

1. Check out the branch containing the F# sibling-window fixture from `fsharp_issue_339_sibling_window_rename`.
2. Run the fixture with the same module name in both files and `--min-nodes 20 --embeddings off`.
3. Compare `window_a.fs:0..524` with `window_b.fs:7..593` through `pair/compare`.
4. Observe that the pair is present in the reported cluster but `pair/compare` returns `admitted: false`.

## Details (for AI)

```shell
# environment
deslop --version: 0.0.0-dev
os: macOS (Darwin, arm64)
surface: pair/compare

# context
fixture: crates/deslop/tests/fsharp_issue_339_sibling_window_rename.rs
min_nodes: 20
embeddings: off
left endpoint: window_a.fs 0..524, 157 nodes
right endpoint: window_b.fs 7..593, 173 nodes

# evidence
production route: shared-subtree rescue
structural overlap S: 0.8786127167630058
token Jaccard J: 0.6875
content agreement A: 0.782608695652174
rename consistency R: 0.0
pair/compare admitted: false
pair/compare explanation: rejected: pair fails the LSH-only guards

# root cause
crates/deslop-core/src/pipeline/session/pair_compare/admission.rs
`rescue_applies` tests `measured.score.bounded_fused() < FUSED_THRESHOLD` after explicit comparison has placed measured S into `score.structural`. Candidate admission instead has structural/Merkle evidence M=0 before rescue, so its pre-rescue fused score is J=0.6875 and rescue is eligible. The explicit path uses S=0.8786127167630058 as pre-rescue evidence, makes rescue false, then `lsh_guard` rejects J below 0.90.
```

## Acceptance Criteria (for AI)

- Add a test comparing `window_a.fs:0..524` (157 nodes) with `window_b.fs:7..593` (173 nodes).
- Assert `S = 0.8786127167630058`, `J = 0.6875`, `A = 0.782608695652174`, and `R = 0.0` without weakening tolerances.
- Assert `admitted = true` and an explanation that names shared-subtree rescue.
- Keep candidate admission and explicit comparison on one admission algebra so measured rescue overlap cannot disqualify its own route.
- Assert the exact sibling-window control remains a hash-route pair at `138/138` nodes with `S = J = A = R = 1.0`.

## Screenshots

None; this is a structured API response.

title: type2_recall and recall_quality lost their evidence clauses to the mass-only wire, with no pair record to replace them
body:
## The defect

The mass-only cluster wire removed every evidence and classification field from `ReportCluster`, and `check_cluster_mass_contract` now actively *forbids* them (`corpus_confidence.rs`, `FORBIDDEN_CLUSTER_FIELDS`: `signals`, `evidence_verdict`, `bucket`, `classification`, …). That is a defensible wire decision. What did not happen is the other half: the rendered report gained no pair record to read that evidence from.

`Report` carries `clusters: Vec<ReportCluster>` and nothing else pair-shaped. `PairComparison` / `PairEvidence` exist in the wire model, but only as the explicit `compare` request/response — they are never part of a rendered report. The corpus gate reads a rendered report. So two curated assertions that used to exist now cannot be made at all:

**1. `type2_recall` no longer asserts gate vouching.** It filtered `gate_vouched(cluster) && cluster_shows_span(cluster, files)`. It now filters on `cluster_shows_span` alone, and `gate_vouched` does not exist anywhere in the tree. The two tests that pinned it — `a_curated_pair_found_but_demoted_is_a_gate_failure` and `a_curated_pair_in_a_sub_floor_near_miss_is_not_vouched_recall` — were deleted, not replaced.

**2. `recall_quality` no longer asserts classification.** `check_one_curated_clone` finds the first spanning visible cluster and applies the rank ceiling. It reads no bucket, because a cluster no longer has one. `[CORPUS-RECALL]` says "`identical` is the only classification a byte-identical pair may reach"; nothing enforces it.

## Why this matters

A curated Type-2 entry now passes on membership + extent + visibility + rank. Those are real assertions — gh #439's two witnesses still fail correctly, and the extent floor does most of the work. But nothing checks that the engine *admitted the pair as a rename*. A cluster that reaches the curated extent and spans both paths passes whether or not the content gate ever vouched for it.

This is a reduction in assertiveness, which `AGENTS.md` prohibits. It is recorded here rather than quietly written into the specs.

## What the docs currently claim

Four places assert more than the code does. They are being corrected to match the code as part of gh #439, with a pointer to this issue:

- `corpus/known-failures.json` `_checks.type2_recall` — "a shown, **gate-vouched** `nearly_identical` cluster"
- `docs/plans/corpus-assertion.md` table row — "curated renames reported, **gate-vouched**, shown … ✅"
- `docs/plans/corpus-assertion.md` §L9 prose — "asks two questions: does a visible cluster span the curated files, **and is it gate-vouched**"
- `docs/specs/corpus.md` `[CORPUS-RECALL]` — "admitted with the required **structural and content evidence** … Assertions read the **pair record** for evidence", and "`identical` is the only classification a byte-identical pair may reach"

## Fix

- [ ] Decide the surface: either the rendered report carries a pair record for curated endpoints, or the gate gains a second read (e.g. driving `compare` on the curated endpoints) that can see admission evidence.
- [ ] Failing test first, in `corpus_confidence/tests/curated.rs`: a curated pair reported at full extent, within its rank ceiling, both occurrences shown, but **never vouched by the content gate**, must raise `type2_recall`. Watch it fail — today it passes.
- [ ] Same for `recall_quality`: a curated byte-identical pair whose endpoints compare as anything other than `identical` must fail.
- [ ] Restore the two deleted `type2_recall` tests against the new surface.
- [ ] Re-point the four documents above at the restored contract.

## Context

Found while auditing gh #439 after merging the mass-only wire branch. gh #439's own items are otherwise complete: the extent floor and the `max_rank` ceiling both land and both are verified to bite against the pinned tokio and nest clones.
