title: JetBrains Gradle Java target does not match 2024.3 platform spec
body:
## Spec violation

`docs/specs/jetbrains.md` says the JetBrains plugin runs on the IntelliJ Platform **2024.3 platform line (build 243) and newer** and identifies that as the build baseline in `[JETBRAINS-TARGET]` / `[JETBRAINS-LSP]`.

## Code observed

Both JetBrains Gradle modules compile with Java 17:

- `clients/jetbrains/deslop-shared/build.gradle.kts`: `kotlin { jvmToolchain(17) }`
- `clients/jetbrains/deslop-lsp4ij/build.gradle.kts`: `kotlin { jvmToolchain(17) }`

During `make jetbrains-package`, the IntelliJ Platform Gradle Plugin reports:

```text
Java sourceCompatibility too low for target platform Java sourceCompatibility is set to '17', but IntelliJ Platform '2024.3' requires Java '21'. This mismatch may prevent your plugin from compiling or using platform APIs correctly. Update sourceCompatibility to '21' in your build configuration.
```

## Expected

The Gradle JVM/toolchain/source compatibility should match the 2024.3 platform requirement, or the spec should explicitly narrow/justify a Java 17 compile target. The current state is internally inconsistent with the supported-platform contract.

## Verification context

Observed while running local CI prep before PR submission:

```text
PATH=/tmp/deslop-ci-bin:/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin make jetbrains-package
```

title: VSIX DUPLICATION panel out of sync with live engine: stale cluster 31b089e ranked #1, absent from CLI + MCP
body:
## Defect: reactive UI shows a stale cluster ranking that diverges from the authoritative engine

The VS Code **DUPLICATION** tree-view (LSP-broadcast) is displaying a cluster set / worst-first ranking that does **not** match the live engine. The reactive loop (watcher → scheduler → session → broadcast → UI) is not converging the panel onto the current generation.

### Observed (same workspace, same moment)

**VS Code DUPLICATION panel** shows rank #1 = cluster `31b089e` — "Identical code", **19 copies** — anchored at:
- `crates/deslop-mcp/tests/issue_137_ipc_freshness.rs:31:79` and `:103:3`
- plus `issue_149_ui_mcp_agreement.rs`, `lsp_integration.rs`, `state_file_backend.rs`, `issue_136_codex_payload_size.rs`, `issue_135_rescan_generation.rs`, `issue_156_cluster_id_stale_offsets.rs`, `issue_153_rescan_freshness.rs`, `dart_generated_fp_over_mcp.rs`
(it is the shared `lsp_workspace_with_socket()? + initialized_mcp(...)?` test-setup block.)

**Cold CLI** — `./target/release/deslop . --no-color` (authoritative, re-analyzes from scratch; this is what the CI duplication gate runs):
- `Found 488 groups`, duplication 22.40%.
- Worst group #1 = **16× `cluster_filters/python_orm.rs, rust.rs, …`** (id `133cc859`, weight 495).
- **No** cluster touches `issue_137_ipc_freshness.rs:31`.

**Live MCP** — `top-offenders` (no path filter, `occurrences_truncated:false`) and `report-for-file crates/deslop-mcp/tests/issue_137_ipc_freshness.rs`:
- Agrees with the CLI: #1 = `133cc859`; `31b089e` not in the top results.
- `report-for-file` for that file returns clusters at lines **49, 100, 113, 138, 146** only — **nothing at line 31**.

### Diagnosis
The CLI and MCP (both re-derive from current source) **agree**; the **VSIX panel is stale** — it retains a previous-generation cluster (`31b089e`) and ranking after the corpus changed. The MCP itself is correct.

### Impact
Violates the core "Deslop.live = the whole loop, including a reactive UI refresh" guarantee and "Consistency across UI panels is critical." A user reading the panel acts on duplication that no longer exists and misses the actual worst offender.

### Expected
After any incremental update, the DUPLICATION panel's cluster set + worst-first ordering must equal the engine's current generation (what `deslop .` and the MCP report). The panel must not display clusters absent from the live generation.

### Repro
1. Open a workspace in the VSIX; note the DUPLICATION panel ranking.
2. Edit/dedup source so the worst-first set changes.
3. Compare the panel against `deslop . --no-color` and MCP `top-offenders`.
4. Panel retains the stale cluster/ranking; CLI + MCP show the new set.

_Filed per CLAUDE.md Rule zero (stale generation / broadcast desync). Detected while deduping the repo; switched dedup ground-truth to the cold CLI + MCP, which agree._

title: Shipwright deployment-contract hardening checklist
body:
Bring the release/IDE deployment into full conformity with the Shipwright contract.

### Version / resolution
- [ ] LSP implements the `--version` contract line — `[SWR-VERSION-CLI-OUTPUT]`
- [ ] `DESLOP_BINARY_DIR` override must **not** bypass exact version comparison — `[SWR-IDE-RESOLUTION]`
- [ ] JetBrains resolution enforces version after finding the binary — `[SWR-IDE-ERROR]`

### Supply-chain hardening (shared controls)
- [ ] SHA-pin every GitHub Actions `uses:` to a 40-char commit (no `@v4`/`@stable`); add `.github/dependabot.yml` to keep pins fresh — `[SWR-SEC-ACTION-PINNING]`
- [ ] Top-level `permissions: contents: read`; grant write / `id-token` / `attestations` per-job only — `[SWR-SEC-TOKEN-PRIVILEGE]`
- [ ] Frozen installs (`npm ci` / `--frozen-lockfile` / `cargo --locked`) — `[SWR-SEC-FROZEN-INSTALL]`
- [ ] Build provenance (`actions/attest-build-provenance`) + CycloneDX SBOM per artifact — `[SWR-SEC-PROVENANCE]`, `[SWR-SEC-SBOM]`
- [ ] One cosign-signed `SHA256SUMS` over all release assets (retire bare per-asset `.sha256`) — `[SWR-SEC-CHECKSUM]`
- [ ] Any downloader (Zed / Neovim / host) verifies checksum **and** signature before executing a fetched binary — `[SWR-SEC-CHECKSUM]`
- [ ] OIDC trusted publishing where supported; retire long-lived registry tokens — `[SWR-SEC-OIDC-PUBLISH]`

---
Tracked as a Shipwright deployment-contract conformity checklist (`SWR-*` IDs). Run the `shipwright-compliance` skill against this repo for the full per-channel audit. These are hardening items, not active exploits.

title: Synchronise selected cluster across editor, Top Offenders, webview, and bubble
body:
## Summary

Lock the editor caret, the Top Offenders panel, the cluster webview, and the live bubble onto a **single selected cluster** so they stay in sync.

Spec: [vsix.md §VSIX-CLUSTER-SYNC](docs/specs/vsix.md) + [§VSIX-CLUSTER-SYNC-TESTS](docs/specs/vsix.md). Tracked in [PLAN.md](docs/plans/PLAN.md). Sibling of #177.

## Behaviour

One `selectedClusterId` signal on the `ReportStore` ([VSIX-STATE]) — the same one decorations/bubble/webview already read. Every surface both writes and reacts to it; no surface keeps a private "current cluster".

**Writers:**
- `deslop.openCluster` ("view cluster" from lens / hover / tree / palette) sets the id before the webview opens.
- Editor caret: `onDidChangeTextEditorSelection` resolves the caret against the visible projection; in-clone → set id, out → clear. Debounced.
- Tree row selection and webview prev/next arrows set it through the same path.

**Reactors:**
- **Top Offenders tree** `effect()` → `TreeView.reveal(node, { select: true, focus: false })`. **Tapping "view cluster" selects the cluster in the panel**, and so does moving the caret into a duplicate. `focus: false` never steals the caret.
- Decorations, bubble, webview already follow the signal.

## Work

- [ ] Add/centralise `selectedClusterId` writes from the editor-caret listener and `deslop.openCluster`.
- [ ] Implement `getParent` on `TopOffendersProvider` (hard requirement of `TreeView.reveal`); resolve the row under cluster/file/folder/language ancestry. No-op (not error) if the cluster isn't in the active projection.
- [ ] Tree `effect()` over `selectedClusterId` → reveal+select.
- [ ] Clear selection in the same microtask if the LSP retracts the cluster ([VSIX-REACTIVITY-INVARIANT]).

## Acceptance (E2E, real LSP + extension host)

Per `[VSIX-CLUSTER-SYNC-TESTS]`, each asserting the **same cluster id** across surfaces:
- `deslop.openCluster` → `topOffendersView.selection[0]` is that cluster — in cluster, file, **and** folder modes (proves `getParent` under nesting).
- Caret into a clone → tree selects that cluster, `window.activeTextEditor` unchanged; caret to a clean line → selection clears.
- Round-trip: editor-driven selection == webview `selectedClusterId` == tree selection.
- Retraction: select, then delete the duplicate; after watcher+scheduler pass, no surface still reports that id.

title: Configurable severity model + diagnostics off by default
body:
## Summary

Replace the hardcoded LSP diagnostic severity (`Identical→Error`, everything else `→Warning`) with a configurable **two-map severity model**, and make clone diagnostics **off by default**.

Spec: [severity.md](docs/specs/severity.md) (new) · [lsp.md §LSP-SEVERITY](docs/specs/lsp.md) · [vsix.md §VSIX-SEVERITY-CONTROL](docs/specs/vsix.md). Tracked in [PLAN.md](docs/plans/PLAN.md).

## Model

Two bucket-keyed maps over `Identical · NearlyIdentical · LooselySimilar · SameBehavior`:

| Map | Setting | Values | Drives | Default |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Deslop severity** (always on) | `deslop.severity.*` | error/warning/information/hint | bubble · tree dot · code-lens · gutter **colour** | Identical=error, NearlyIdentical=warning, LooselySimilar=information, SameBehavior=hint |
| **Diagnostic severity** (opt-in) | `deslop.diagnostics.severity.*` | + `none` | **Problems panel / squiggle** | coincides with above |
| **Master gate** | `deslop.diagnostics.enabled` | bool | whether diagnostics publish at all | **`false` (OFF)** |

- Diagnostics are **off by default**; the always-on bubble + tree carry the loudness. This deliberately reverses the old "never silent by default" stance in `[LSP-SEVERITY-BUCKET]`.
- Colour is independent of the gate — bubbles stay fully coloured with diagnostics off.
- A bucket can be set to `none` to suppress its Problems entries while staying visible/coloured.
- The two maps may diverge (e.g. Identical shows red but publishes only `warning` to avoid breaking an error-gated CI lint).
- Colour vs. percentile are orthogonal channels: colour = which bucket; glyph `●●/●/◐/○` = weight percentile.

## Work

- [ ] `crates/deslop-lsp/src/diagnostics.rs`: resolve `gate_enabled → bucket → severity (≠none) → percentile-floor → publish/suppress`. Single source of truth.
- [ ] `clients/vscode/src/severity.ts`: `resolveSeverity(bucket, percentile) → { color, glyph }`, the only place either channel is computed.
- [ ] `package.json`: add `deslop.diagnostics.enabled` (default `false`), `deslop.severity.*`, `deslop.diagnostics.severity.*` (all `scope: window`), forwarded to the LSP on `initialize` + `didChangeConfiguration`.
- [ ] UI (`[VSIX-SEVERITY-CONTROL]`): prominent toggle at `navigation@0` of the Top Offenders title bar (`$(bell-slash)`↔`$(bell)`, `when` on `deslop:diagnosticsEnabled`), dismissible header note, clickable status-bar mirror, and a `deslop.severity.configure` QuickPick editing both maps in flow.
- [ ] Update bubble/lens colour wiring to read the always-on Deslop map, not the diagnostic projection.

## Acceptance (E2E, real LSP + extension host)

Per `[severity.md §SEVERITY-TESTING]`:
- Default posture: Problems empty, tree+bubble populated & coloured (Identical→red).
- Gate on → `Identical=Error`, others `Warning`; gate off clears all.
- `deslop.diagnostics.severity.identical = none` drops Problems entries, colour unchanged.
- `deslop.severity.sameBehavior = error` repaints bubble red without touching Problems.
- Decoupling: `severity.identical=error` + `diagnostics.severity.identical=warning` → red bubble, `Warning` diagnostic.

title: VSIX showstopper: "Open Cluster Details" renders a blank panel on large/active repos — selection latches a volatile content-hash cluster id against a live, churning report (silent, no diagnostic)
body:
## Summary

On a large, actively-analyzed repository, the VSIX "Open Cluster Details" command almost always renders a blank panel reading "No cluster selected." instead of the cluster the user clicked. The panel captures the cluster id at click time but is fed the latest live snapshot, and because a cluster's id is a content hash that churns when the codebase changes, the captured id no longer resolves in the snapshot the freshly-mounted webview receives. This is a showstopper because it breaks core UX precisely on the codebases Deslop exists to serve — large, continuously-edited, agent-driven repos — while appearing to "work" on tiny demo repos, and it fails silently with no diagnostic.

## Repro

1. Open a large repository under live Deslop analysis (LSP active, agent or human actively writing files to disk).
2. Open the Deslop report tree and let it populate with clusters.
3. Right-click any cluster row → **Open Cluster Details** while edits/rescans are ongoing.
4. Observe: the panel opens but renders `No cluster selected.` (`clients/vscode/webview-ui/src/cluster/main.tsx:67-73`).
5. Repeat on a tiny, idle fixture repo: the panel reliably shows the cluster.

**Expected:** opening details on any visible cluster always shows that cluster.
**Actual:** on a large/active repo the panel is blank almost every time; on a tiny idle repo it works, which masks the bug in demos and CI.

## Root cause

The failure is the composition of an unstable identity, a capture-once/push-latest race, a dirty-projection feed, and rescan churn — with no diagnostic to expose any of it.

**1. The cluster id is content-derived, not a stable handle.** `materialize_cluster` sets `id: encode_short_id(cluster_id_source(&members))` (`crates/deslop-core/src/cluster.rs:138-140`), where `cluster_id_source` returns the minimum member's blake3 normalized-AST hash:

```rust
fn cluster_id_source(members: &[Fingerprint]) -> [u8; 32] {
    members
        .iter()
        .min_by_key(|member| member.hash)
        .map_or([0_u8; 32], |member| member.hash)
}
```
(`crates/deslop-core/src/cluster.rs:184-190`; `Fingerprint.hash` is the normalized subtree digest, `crates/deslop-core/src/fingerprint.rs:19-21`). The id is stable only for an *identical* member set across runs (`crates/deslop-core/src/cluster.rs:49-51`). It changes whenever the min-hash member's normalized hash changes, a smaller-hash member joins, or the min-hash member leaves — i.e. on content/membership mutation of the canonical occurrence. It is not a positional handle.

**2. Panel captures the id once but pushes the latest snapshot, and the webview resolves by exact id-or-null with no fallback.** `openClusterPanel` posts `select/cluster` exactly once, inside a one-shot `ready` handler that disposes after firing (`clients/vscode/src/webview/panels.ts:33-35`, `102-109`):

```ts
const unsub = wirePanel(panel, store, "cluster", (webview) => {
  void webview.postMessage({ kind: "select/cluster", id: clusterId });
});
```
Meanwhile the snapshot feed continuously pushes the latest report on every store change (`clients/vscode/src/webview/panels.ts:91-101`). The webview sets `selectedClusterId` only on `select/cluster` and never re-derives it from a snapshot (`clients/vscode/webview-ui/src/store.ts:72-82`), then resolves with a strict exact match and a hard `null` fallback:

```ts
export const selectedCluster = computed<ReportCluster | null>(() => {
  const id = selectedClusterId.value;
  if (!id) return null;
  return clusters.value.find((c) => c.id === id) ?? null;
});
```
(`clients/vscode/webview-ui/src/store.ts:39-43`). A miss renders the blank state (`clients/vscode/webview-ui/src/cluster/main.tsx:67-73`) and there is no occurrence/path-based re-resolution. `activePanels` is keyed `cluster:${clusterId}` (`clients/vscode/src/webview/panels.ts:29-31`), so once the id churns, reveal/dedup also break — the same cluster under a new id is a different map entry.

**3. The panel is fed the dirty `visibleReport` projection, not canonical `report`.** The push subscribes to `store.visibleReport.value` (`clients/vscode/src/webview/panels.ts:91-101`), the dirty-aware projection that drops any cluster whose visible occurrence count falls below two during active editing — `if (kept.length < 2) continue;` (`clients/vscode/src/reportStore.ts:187-195`). This violates the store's own documented contract that cluster-id lookups for commands like `openCluster` are honoured against canonical truth through unsaved edits (`clients/vscode/src/reportStore.ts:8-18`). A 2-occurrence cluster with one occurrence in the edited file is elided by a single dirty file, blanking the panel via a *still-valid* id — a second, independent path to the same blank render.

**4. Why it scales with repo size.** The watcher → debounce → single-flight scheduler → session loop coarsens but still produces frequent generations under real write activity: a pass fires after 250 ms quiet (`QUIET_MS`) or every 2 s under continuous writes (`CAP_MS`) (`crates/deslop-core/src/live/debouncer.rs:16-19`), each bumping the generation and re-running the pipeline (`crates/deslop-core/src/live/session.rs:389-392`). `applyDelta` is a pure id-keyed merge — removed ids are deleted, added/updated ids set (`clients/vscode/src/reportStore.ts:118-123`) — so a churned cluster arrives as `removed old-id` + `added new-id` and old id X simply vanishes from the canonical store. Larger, agent-driven repos flush files to disk faster, so more generations land inside the small window between a tree-command dispatch and the panel's first snapshot; a tiny idle repo rarely rescans in that window.

**5. No diagnostic anywhere on this surface.** The captured id flows straight through `clusterIdForTreeNode` → `openClusterPanel` → `select/cluster` → webview with zero validation against the live report. There is no `console.log`, no `logWarn`, no `vscode.window.show*`, and no Rust-side tracing on this path (`deslop.lsp.openCluster` only builds a `deslop://cluster/{id}` URI without resolving the id). The one guard, "no cluster resolved for this tree row" (`clients/vscode/src/commands/register.ts:110-118`), fires only when the tree node yields *no id at all*, not when a captured id later fails to match. Note the parallel virtual-document surface *does* diagnose this (`clients/vscode/src/clusterDocument.ts:26-30,60-67` logs `cluster document missing` and renders an explanatory message; the Rust path returns `LiveError::UnknownCluster`, `crates/deslop-core/src/live/errors.rs:65`) — the panel path is the gap.

**Sequence that breaks:**
1. Tree renders a row carrying captured cluster id X (gen N).
2. User invokes Open Cluster Details; the panel begins mounting.
3. A file write lands; generation N+1 re-clusters and churns X's min-hash member → X becomes Y (or X is dirty-elided from `visibleReport`).
4. On `ready`, the panel posts `select/cluster {id: X}`; the snapshot feed pushes the gen N+1 report, which contains Y, not X.
5. `selectedCluster` finds no X → `null` → panel renders `No cluster selected.` and never recovers (navigation requires a non-null selection).

## Why this is the reactivity issue, not a one-off

This is the `[VSIX-STATE]` / `[VSIX-STATE-DIRTY]` reactivity contract breaking in two reinforcing ways. First, the *display's captured id lags the store*: selection is latched once at mount (`select/cluster`, posted from the one-shot `ready` handler) while the report behind it advances generation by generation — the classic stale-handle-against-a-live-store reactivity bug. Second, the handle *itself is volatile*: the short id is a content hash of the min-hash member, so even perfect reactivity on the id value can't help once the id it points at no longer exists. The fix must therefore restore reactivity (re-resolve selection on every snapshot) *and* anchor it to a stable identity, not patch a single render.

## Impact / blast radius

Sibling features split cleanly by which projection they resolve the captured id against:

- **Silently no-op / blank (resolve against the dirty `visibleReport` projection):**
  - The **Cluster Details panel** itself — the reported bug (`clients/vscode/src/webview/panels.ts:33-35,91-101` → `clients/vscode/webview-ui/src/store.ts:39-43`).
  - The TS-side **`deslop://cluster/{id}` virtual document** — also renders from `visibleReport` (`clients/vscode/src/clusterDocument.ts:16-30`); degrades to an explanatory `missingClusterDocument` message rather than a blank panel, so the same churn family but a softer failure.
- **Robust (resolve the captured id against canonical `store.current.report`):** `deslop.copyClusterContextById` (`clients/vscode/src/commands/register.ts:101-108`), `deslop.compareWithCanonical` via `compareCluster` (`register.ts:325-330`), `jumpToNextOccurrence` (`register.ts:189-234`), and the Rust LSP virtual-document handler (`crates/deslop-lsp/src/custom_methods.rs:350-356`), which returns `UnknownCluster` only when the cluster is truly gone.

The asymmetry is the actionable insight: a captured id is meant to be a stable handle, so **id resolution should hit canonical `report`** and only the *rendered occurrence rows* should honour the dirty projection — exactly what the robust commands already do. The cluster panel and the TS cluster virtual doc are the two surfaces that violate this.

**Relation to #171:** related, not a duplicate. #171 is the same `[VSIX-STATE-DIRTY]` mechanism on a different surface (the compact hover card never *appears* over an actively-edited squiggle because `provideHover` finds no occurrence in `visibleReport`). This bug is one level downstream: the tree/card *did* hand a captured `cluster.id` to `deslop.openCluster`, the panel *opens*, but the webview can't resolve the id and blanks. Cross-link, do not merge.

## Fixes (two parts)

**Part A — Defensive diagnostic (do this first).** When the captured id cannot be resolved against the current report, stop failing silently:
- In the **panel host** (`openClusterPanel`, `clients/vscode/src/webview/panels.ts`), validate `clusterId` against `store.current.report` before/at send and on each snapshot; when it is absent, emit a structured log/trace (`cluster no longer exists`, with the stale id and the current generation) and surface a non-blocking `vscode.window.showWarningMessage`.
- In the **webview**, render a distinct "cluster no longer in report" state instead of the generic `No cluster selected.` (`clients/vscode/webview-ui/src/cluster/main.tsx:67-73`), mirroring what `clusterDocument.ts` already does for the virtual-document surface.
- On the **Rust LSP** `open_cluster` path, resolve the id (it currently only formats a URI) so a stale id produces `UnknownCluster` and a tracing event rather than a no-op.

**Part B — The real fix so it never happens.** Make selection survive re-clustering. Options, strongest first:
- **(i) Re-resolve the selection on every snapshot by a stable key (recommended).** Anchor selection to a stable cluster identity — e.g. the canonical occurrence `path` + byte-range of the selected occurrence — rather than the volatile short id, and re-derive `selectedCluster` from each incoming snapshot. This survives id churn *and* restores reactivity in one move.
- **(ii) Re-send `select/cluster` after each snapshot, mapping old→new id via the delta** (`clusters_removed`/`clusters_added`/`clusters_updated`) so the latched id is rewritten when a cluster's id flips.
- **(iii) Feed the cluster panel canonical `report`, not `visibleReport`,** and guard the selected cluster against dirty elision (re-inject it from canonical), aligning with the store's documented "commands go through canonical separately" intent.
- **(iv) Key `activePanels` by a stable identity,** not `cluster:${clusterId}`, so reveal/dedup survive id churn.

Recommended combination: (iii) to feed canonical truth, plus (i) to re-resolve selection by stable key on every snapshot, plus (iv) for panel dedup. **Acceptance bar:** opening details on *any* visible cluster ALWAYS shows that cluster, even under continuous rescans and active dirty edits.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Opening details on any cluster on a large, continuously-rescanning repo always shows that cluster (never `No cluster selected.`).
- [ ] The panel re-resolves/refreshes the selected cluster across generations (id churn no longer blanks it).
- [ ] The dirty-file path (#171-adjacent) is covered: a cluster with an occurrence in an actively-edited file still renders in the panel.
- [ ] `activePanels` reveal/dedup survives id churn (re-opening the same logical cluster reveals the existing panel).
- [ ] A structured diagnostic (log/trace with stale id + current generation) is emitted on any unresolved id, and the user sees a non-blocking message + a distinct webview state — never a silent blank.
- [ ] A black-box E2E test drives the CLI/extension end-to-end against a fixture repo (no fake LSP, per testing rules), forces a generation to land between tree-render and panel-mount (id churn), and asserts the panel shows the cluster; a sibling test covers the dirty-file elision path.

## Related

- #171 — same `[VSIX-STATE-DIRTY]` dirty-projection mechanism, distinct hover-card surface (related, cross-link, not a duplicate).
- #129 — adjacent diagnostic-vs-surface visibility divergence (related context, different gap).

title: VSIX: duplicate hover card (Compare / View cluster / Copy for AI) missing while a file is being edited — only the LSP diagnostic remains
body:
## TL;DR

While you are typing in a file, the popup that carries the clone actions — Compare, View cluster, Copy for AI — disappears. The red underline and its "Identical code × N" message stay. Save the file, and the popup comes back. So the duplicate is flagged exactly while you are editing it, but the buttons to act on it are gone.

## Details

Hovering a piece of duplicated code normally shows two things together: the message "this code is duplicated, here is the original", and a small card with three links — Compare with canonical, View cluster, Copy for AI. Those links are the only way to act on a duplicate straight from the editor.

The moment you type a single character without saving, the card vanishes. The underline and message stay, pointing at a duplicate you can no longer do anything about from the hover. Save the file and everything comes back.

Why: the underline comes straight from the analysis engine and is not affected by unsaved edits. The card is built from a "visible report" that deliberately hides the file you are editing until you save — a rule meant to stop stale information, which accidentally also hides the card. This affects every language, not just Dart; it was first noticed in a Dart file.

Also found while investigating (separate small gap): Deslop watches the disk for `.cs`, `.rs`, and `.py` files but not `.dart` — so changes made to Dart files outside the editor go unnoticed until the next save.

## Steps To Reproduce

1. Open a file that is one copy of a duplicate that also exists in another file. Confirm the hover shows the card with the three links.
2. Type one character. Do not save.
3. Hover the underlined region: the "Identical code × N" message appears, but the card with the links is gone.
4. Save the file. After the analysis catches up, hover again: the card is back.

## Details (for AI)

```shell
# environment
surface: vsix
first observed: integration_test/real_service_tests/chat_test_harness.dart — "Identical code × 5", canonical chat_stop_card_play_test.dart(104, 9)

# expected vs actual
expected: clusterHoverMarkdown(cluster, { showCategory: false }) card (**{slug}** x {count} / Canonical / Compare · View cluster · Copy for AI) rendered alongside the LSP diagnostic
actual:   diagnostic only (message + "Canonical" relatedInformation); host-language hover still renders — popup itself works

# root cause (code-confirmed)
diagnostics:  pushed by Rust LSP via textDocument/publishDiagnostics; NO TS-side publishing (no createDiagnosticCollection / new vscode.Diagnostic in clients/vscode/src); not projection-gated; persist until re-analysis on save
hover card:   ClusterHoverProvider.provideHover (clients/vscode/src/decorations/clusterHoverProvider.ts:15-28) reads store.current.visibleReport — dirty-aware projection; requires sameFile(path, activePath) && byteRangeToRange(doc, occ).contains(position)
dirty wiring: wireDirtyDocuments (clients/vscode/src/extension.ts:411-413) -> markFileDirty(activePath); projectVisible (clients/vscode/src/reportStore.ts:58-60,138-149 [VSIX-STATE-DIRTY]) elides the dirty file's occurrence; cluster survives (other 4 occurrences >= 2) but active file has no matching occurrence -> provideHover returns null -> no card
decorations: DecorationManager underline (clients/vscode/src/decorations/manager.ts:51-58) gated the same way — also vanishes until save
LSP hover:   deliberately suppressed (HOVER_SUPPRESSING_MIDDLEWARE, clients/vscode/src/extension.ts:65-67,278) — TS provider is the only card source
language-agnostic: wireDirtyDocuments/projectVisible apply to every supported language (C#/Rust/Python too)

# suggested direction (not prescriptive)
- ClusterHoverProvider falls back to the canonical report for the active file, or skip eliding the active file's own occurrence for hover/decoration; or
- suppress the LSP diagnostic for dirty files so both views clear together

# separate confirmed gap
synchronize.fileEvents watcher glob is **/*.{cs,rs,py} (clients/vscode/src/extension.ts:272) — omits .dart although dart is in ANALYSED_DOCUMENTS and the selector (extension.ts:53-58); should be **/*.{cs,rs,py,dart}; introduced when Dart support landed (#161)

# spec ids
[VSIX-HOVER-SHARED] [VSIX-STATE-DIRTY]
related issues: #161
```

## Acceptance Criteria (for AI)

- While a file is dirty (typed-in, unsaved), hovering a duplicated region shows **both** the LSP diagnostic **and** the compact card with Compare / View cluster / Copy for AI links.
- The DecorationManager underline and the hover card appear and disappear together with the diagnostic under the dirty projection.
- The `synchronize.fileEvents` watcher glob includes `.dart`.
- Reproduces for C#/Rust/Python files, not just Dart.

title: Dart grammar: experimental declarative-constructor syntax (`new name(...) : init`) produces ERROR nodes
body:
## TL;DR

Deslop cannot parse one very new piece of Dart syntax — a special short form for writing constructors — so those spots show up as unparsed in the scan. It only appears in the Dart team's own unreleased code, so almost no real user will hit it. Nothing crashes; the rest of the file is still analysed.

## Details

Deslop reads Dart code using a parser library (tree-sitter-dart). That library does not yet understand one experimental syntax: a constructor declared with `new name(...) :` followed by setup assignments.

How do we know it's just this one gap? A file exercising all of modern Dart 3 — records, patterns, sealed classes, enums, async generators, and more — parses perfectly. A sweep of 2,372 real files across the Flutter and Dart SDK repos came back 99.59% clean, and every real-code failure was this same construct. No crashes anywhere: the parser recovers and keeps going.

Where it shows up: only inside the Dart SDK's own tryouts of the unreleased feature. You have to opt in with `--enable-experiment` to even write this syntax, so no released app contains it.

Severity: low. This is a tracking issue — fix it by updating the parser library when it adds support.

Found while stress-testing Dart support against flutter/flutter, flutter/packages, and dart-lang/sdk.

## Steps To Reproduce

1. Save this one-line Dart file:

   ```dart
   class A { final int x; final int y; new _(this.x) : y = 1; }
   ```

2. Run `deslop --debug-ast <file>.dart` (or scan a folder containing it).
3. Observe: the constructor line produces an ERROR node — the parser does not understand `new _(...) : y = 1`.
4. Compare: the same constructor without the assignment part — `new _(this.x);` — parses fine. The trigger is the `: assignment` list on a `new`-style constructor.

## Details (for AI)

```shell
# environment
grammar: tree-sitter-dart, nielsenko fork, pinned 0.2.0
trigger: initializer list on a `new`-declared constructor (experimental declarative-constructor syntax)

# bisect table
new _(this.x);                     -> clean
new _(super.x);                    -> clean
new _({required super.x});         -> clean
new named(this.x);                 -> clean
new _(this.x) : y = 1;             -> ERROR
A._(this.x) : y = 1; (standard)    -> clean

# evidence
sweep: 2,372 real files (flutter/flutter, flutter/packages, dart-lang/sdk; excluding intentionally-malformed parser test corpora) -> 99.59% production clean-parse
real-code failures: ~8, all this construct, plus one deliberate `//# compile-time error` test
dart 3.x feature stress file (records, patterns, sealed/base/final/interface classes, extension types, enhanced enums, async*/sync*, null-aware collection elements, cascades, typedefs, adjacent strings, symbols): 0 ERROR nodes
crashes: none — error recovery degrades to ERROR nodes that flow through the pipeline harmlessly; file still analysed

# affected files (dart-lang/sdk, unreleased-feature dogfooding)
  - pkg/analysis_server/lib/src/lsp/lsp_analysis_server.dart
  - pkg/analysis_server/lib/src/utilities/element_location2.dart

# severity
low: requires --enable-experiment; SDK-internal only; tracking issue for grammar pin bump
```

## Acceptance Criteria (for AI)

- Parsing `class A { final int x; final int y; new _(this.x) : y = 1; }` yields **0 ERROR nodes**.
- The two affected SDK files parse clean.
- The Dart 3.x feature stress file still yields 0 ERROR nodes (no regression from the grammar bump).

## Screenshots

None.

title: Performance: CLI analysis is single-threaded and holds whole corpus in RAM (~9.5 GB / 9m44s on flutter/flutter)
body:
## Summary

Cold-cache CLI analysis is **single-threaded** and **holds the whole corpus + fingerprints in RAM**. On large real-world Dart codebases this means multi-minute runs and multi-GB memory. Measured while benchmarking the Dart implementation:

| Repo | Dart files | Analysed LOC | Wall | CPU (user/real) | Peak RSS |
|------|-----------:|-------------:|-----:|-----------------|---------:|
| `flutter/packages` | 2,366 | 957k | 104s | 101s / 104s | 4.5 GB |
| `flutter/flutter`  | 6,473 | 2.51M | **584s (9m44s)** | 547s / 584s | **9.56 GB** |
| `dart-lang/sdk` `sdk/lib` | 481 | 264k | 21s | 20s / 21s | 2.9 GB |

## Observations

1. **Single-threaded.** `user ≈ real` on every run (flutter: 547s user vs 584s real). The embarrassingly-parallel per-file work (tree-sitter parse + subtree fingerprint) pins one core while the rest idle. A 6.4k-file repo shouldn't take ~10 minutes on a modern multi-core machine.
2. **Memory scales with corpus size.** ~9.5 GB on Flutter; extrapolating, the full `dart-lang/sdk` (~25k Dart files) would likely exceed 30 GB and OOM. I deliberately ran only a bounded `sdk/lib` slice to avoid taking the machine down.

## Why it matters / why it might not

- The **live LSP/MCP path** (the flagship product) is incremental and per-file, so this is much less relevant there.
- The **CLI cold-cache path** is the documented CI-gate / one-shot-audit fallback. On a large monorepo, a 10-minute single-threaded run with a 9.5 GB working set is a real scalability ceiling.

## Recommended direction

- Parallelise the per-file parse + fingerprint stage (e.g. `rayon` over the file list) — the stage is independent per file until clustering.
- Consider a streaming / bounded-memory fingerprint store so peak RSS scales sub-linearly with corpus size, enabling whole-SDK-scale runs.

## Severity

**Medium, not a showstopper.** Correctness is unaffected; this is throughput/footprint. It does, however, currently make whole-Dart-SDK-scale analysis impractical.

---
Found while stress-testing the Dart implementation against flutter/flutter, flutter/packages, and dart-lang/sdk.

Two related changes to the VSIX tree view, driven by real usage:

Current tree sections are: **Top Offenders**, **Focused File**, **Session** (Embedding model / Cache / Files analysed / State). The _Focused File_ section earns no real estate. title: LSP diagnostics only show for open files — add 'always display' workspace mode
body:
## Problem

Diagnostics for duplicate-code clusters are currently only visible in the editor's Problems panel **while the host file is open**. The moment the user closes the tab, the diagnostics for that file disappear. The Top Offenders tree still lists every offender, but the corresponding squiggles and Problems entries vanish unless the user re-opens each file.

This is a direct consequence of the LSP's **pull-based** diagnostic model: `crates/deslop-lsp/src/backend.rs::diagnostic` (LSP 3.17 `textDocument/diagnostic`) only publishes diagnostics when the editor pulls them — and editors pull only for files they have open. There is no `publishDiagnostics` push for unopened files in the workspace.

## Repro

1. Open a workspace with known duplicates (e.g. the AiCms test suite).
2. Open `EndpointWorkflowTests.cs` — Problems panel populates with 51 deslop entries. ✅
3. Switch to a different tab so `EndpointWorkflowTests.cs` is closed — its 51 entries vanish from Problems. ❌

Expected (in 'always display' mode): every offender in the workspace stays in Problems regardless of which tab is focused, matching the Top Offenders tree.

## Fix

Add a workspace-scoped configuration item that flips the LSP between two diagnostic modes:

- `\"open-files\"` (current behaviour, default) — pull-based, only diagnoses files the editor opens. Cheap, low noise, matches LSP 3.17 default.
- `\"workspace\"` — LSP actively pushes `textDocument/publishDiagnostics` for **every** file with at least one cluster occurrence after each pipeline pass, so Problems shows the full set even with no tabs open.

### Surfaces to wire

- **Spec:** new section in `docs/specs/lsp.md` under `[LSP-DIAGNOSTICS]` — call it `[LSP-DIAGNOSTICS-SCOPE]`. Document both modes, defaults, and the push contract for `workspace`.
- **Core / LSP:** `LspBackend` reads the new setting at `initialize` (and on `workspace/didChangeConfiguration`); the scheduler's post-pass broadcast either continues to push only `deslop/reportChanged` (open-files) or also fans out `publishDiagnostics` per offender file (workspace).
- **VSIX:** new key in `clients/vscode/package.json` → `contributes.configuration`:
  - id: `deslop.diagnostics.scope`
  - type: `string`
  - enum: `[\"open-files\", \"workspace\"]`
  - default: `\"open-files\"`
  - description: \"Which files publish diagnostics. 'open-files' (default) only diagnoses files open in the editor; 'workspace' pushes diagnostics for every file with a duplicate occurrence so Problems stays populated even with no tabs open.\"
- **JetBrains:** mirror the same setting via the existing settings panel.
- **Tests:** E2E in `crates/deslop-lsp/tests/` — open fixture workspace in `workspace` scope, assert `publishDiagnostics` arrives for files the client never opened; in `open-files` scope, assert no `publishDiagnostics` for unopened files.

## Notes

- This is an additive, opt-in change — default behaviour stays pull-based to avoid surprising users with thousands of unopened-file diagnostics.
- Push path must respect [LSP-PUSH] correctness: every re-analysis pass refreshes the published set; deletions clear stale diagnostics.
- Related: [LSP-DIAGNOSTICS], [LSP-PUSH] in `docs/specs/lsp.md`.

## Screenshots

![With file open — 51 diagnostics in Problems panel](https://example.invalid/file-open.png)
![Same file closed — diagnostics gone, only Top Offenders tree remains](https://example.invalid/file-closed.png)

title: After-action: dedup session report — what worked, what broke, what to fix first
body:
## Honest read on a real session

I (LLM agent) ran a multi-hour dedup pass on a 26K-LOC Python codebase. End state: **9 real refactors landed**, **354 → ~70 clusters** (most of the drop was the embedding pass collapsing things, not real fixes), and **103 tests still green**. Here's what I'd want fixed first if I were doing this again tomorrow.

### Wins (please don't break)

- **Pre-embedding-pass `nearly_identical` was the most useful signal.** Every real refactor I landed came from a cluster with `structural≥0.95, token≥0.95, occurrence_count∈[2,5]`. Those clusters were tractable, byte ranges fit in a single `Read` call per occurrence, and the canonical AST normalization made renamed-identifier clones visible without false-flagging unrelated functions.
- **`top-offenders` and `cluster-by-id` are gold.** They give exactly what I need to action: id, signals, occurrences, weight. No bloat. Keep them as the primary entry points.
- **The new `schema-doc` standalone tool fixed the worst per-call cost from #111/#116.** Reports no longer ship 10KB of tutorial text. This is a big win — please don't regress it.
- **`rescan` after every edit works fast enough** to keep the loop tight.

### What hurt

In rough order of pain:

1. **Embedding pass produces a 188-file mega-cluster that hides real wins.** Filed as #120. This is the single highest-impact regression — `report-query --bucket=nearly_identical` returns empty on our codebase post-embedding-pass, even though there were ~10 actionable Type-3 clones in there.
2. **Byte offsets, no line numbers in `occurrences[]`.** Filed in #116. Every cluster requires byte→line conversion before I can `Read` the code. With 5+ occurrences per cluster, that's 5× the tool calls. Please add `start_line`/`end_line` — tree-sitter has them.
3. **No `path_excludes` filter.** Filed in #116. I want \"src/ but NOT tests/\". Have to scroll past test FPs.
4. **No way to mark patterns as acceptable.** Filed in #100, #103, #107, #112, #114, #121. SQLAlchemy column declarations, Pydantic schema mirrors, pytest density patterns, pytest fixture idioms, JWT independent re-implementation, etc. — all canonical patterns that cluster forever and need a `.deslop.toml`-level annotation, per-cluster suppression, or decorator-aware demotion.
5. **No `report-diff <cluster_id>` tool.** Filed in #116. To verify an `Identical` cluster I have to `Read` both files manually. A tool that returns the canonical occurrence + a unified diff against each other occurrence would 5× verification speed.
6. **TMC 200-char message cap.** Hard-coded ceiling means coordination messages get truncated. This is bundled with the dedup workflow so worth raising even though it's a TMC issue not deslop.

### What I want most

If you fix exactly **one** thing: **stop the embedding pass from absorbing structural matches** (#120). The pre-embedding behaviour was net-positive for agent productivity. The embedding-on behaviour is net-negative because the wins it claims to find don't get surfaced; they get fused into noise.

If you fix exactly **two** things: that, plus **`start_line`/`end_line` in occurrences** (#116). Halves my tool-call count per cluster.

### Stuff I deliberately did NOT file

- The action_hints array in every report-query response (~600 chars, redundant with the schema-doc tool). Tolerable; not worth a ticket on its own.
- Visual VSIX showing 350 \"clusters\" most of which are FPs. That's a UX problem on top of #100/#103/#107/#112/#114/#121 being unfixed at the engine layer; fix the engine and the VSIX cleans up.

### Closing

The tool *can* find real duplication. Most of my wins this session would not have surfaced with a hand-grep — the AST normalization + cross-file matching genuinely paid off. But the embedding pass currently turns those wins invisible. Untrust embedding-only edges, ship the line numbers, give me a `path_excludes` filter, and the next agent's session is 3× more productive.

title: Tool UX report from heavy MCP-driven dedup session: which tools were useful, which were useless, what blocked progress
body:
This is feedback from a long agent-driven dedup session that killed 76 clusters (462→386, ~16%) and filed 6 false-positive issues (#98–#106). Roughly 30+ Deslop MCP calls across multiple `/loop` iterations.

## Tools that worked well (need to keep)

### `cluster-by-id`
Essential. The inspection workflow is "scan top → pick a cluster id → look at all its occurrences." Returning the full `occurrences[]` list with byte ranges is exactly what the agent needs to grep into source. No complaints.

### `rescan` with `paths`
Critical. After every batch of edits I called `rescan(paths=[...])` and got fresh state. Watcher lag would have been a deal-breaker; manual rescan is the right escape hatch. Suggestion: surface `total_clusters` more prominently — agents anchor on it as the "score."

### `report-query`
The `offset` + `bucket` filter is essential to dig past the FP-saturated top-15. Most of the actionable wins this session came from offsets 15–35.

## Tools I never used (consider removing or documenting better)

### `find-similar`
Zero calls in this session. The intended workflow seems to be "before writing new code, check if it's a clone of existing code." But agents in dedup mode are *fixing existing dupes*, not authoring fresh code. The doc says "Call before writing to avoid introducing new clones" — but agents don't normally re-read doc strings mid-session, and there's no nudge in the report output. **Consider promoting this in the report's `action_hints` block, or removing it.**

### `session-config`
Zero calls. The metadata it returns (root, min-nodes, languages, generation) is also embedded in `report-query`'s response. Truly redundant. **Suggest removing or merging into report metadata.**

### `report-get` (vs `report-query`)
I used `report-query` exclusively; `report-get` returns the same shape minus filters. **Consider deprecating in favor of `report-query` with optional filters.**

## What hurt productivity

### Massive `schema_doc` payload on every call (BIG)
**Every** `report-query`/`top-offenders`/`report-get` response includes a ~10KB `schema_doc` field with a full markdown explanation of how Deslop works — buckets, signals, routing tables, etc. This is repeated **on every paginated call**. After the first call the agent already knows; on call #20 it's 200KB of dead weight.

**Fix:** add `include_schema_doc: bool = False` (or `terse: true`) to suppress it. Or send it only on first call per session. This is the #1 friction point — every tool result eats a huge chunk of the agent's context window.

### `top-offenders` is mostly a duplicate of `report-query offset=0`
The "n=8" version is convenient but the schema_doc bloat applies here too. The action_hints array is also re-sent every call.

### Cluster IDs aren't always stable across edits
A cluster ID changed across passes (e.g. `03767d72` resurfaced with different byte ranges + slightly different signals after I edited an adjacent test). The doc says "Same clone across runs → same id" — but moving lines around (which is what dedup *does*) flips the canonical-id selection. **Document the stability contract more precisely**: "id stable as long as the canonical occurrence's *content* is unchanged" or similar.

### `report-query` doesn't expose a per-cluster permalink
After an edit that shifted byte offsets, looking up the *previous* cluster id sometimes hit "no cluster with id." A "cluster history" endpoint or stable-by-content lookup would help loops that are iterating over a fixed shortlist.

### No way to mark "I've reviewed this cluster as a known FP"
Out of the top 15, ~5–7 are persistent false positives I've already filed (#98, #99, #100, #104, #105, #106). They keep returning to the top of the report. **Suggest a `.deslop.toml` `[ignore] cluster_ids = [...]` or per-cluster `wontfix` annotation** so reviewers can demote known-FP clusters without having to re-read them every loop iteration.

## Doc gaps

- **`min_size` filter behavior with size=2 clusters**: `report-query` with `min_size=3` is what I converged on after noticing tons of `size=2` noise. The default min_size isn't well-documented; the doc says "size 2 with low weight is usually boilerplate" but doesn't say "use min_size=3 to filter."
- **`paths` in `rescan`**: must they be absolute, workspace-relative, or either? I sent workspace-relative and it worked, but I had to guess.
- **Generation counter**: the `generation` field in responses is undocumented. Useful or noise?

## Adjacent broken tool (not Deslop, FYI)

`mcp__too-many-cooks__status` returns ~310KB of output that exceeds the agent's max-tokens-per-tool-result. **Unusable at any non-trivial scale.** Filed only as cross-reference because the dedup-coordination workflow tries to use it.

## Adjacent issue: Basilisk false positives drown every Edit

Every single `Edit` to a test file triggers a basilisk diagnostic: `Cannot resolve import 'tests.helpers'` or `Cannot resolve import 'agent_backend.*'`. These are pre-existing false positives — but they spam the agent's PostToolUse feedback channel. Each Edit costs ~500 tokens of stale linter complaints. Not Deslop's bug, but worth knowing the editing experience suffers from cumulative tool-noise. (Already tracked elsewhere I assume.)

## TL;DR — top 3 asks

1. **Add `include_schema_doc: false` (or auto-suppress after first call).** Biggest single context-window saver.
2. **Document/implement a way to mute persistent false-positive clusters.** Otherwise the report's "top 15" fossilizes around FPs.
3. **Either promote `find-similar` in the workflow or remove it.** Currently dead code from the agent's POV.

title: Tool usage report: which deslop MCP tools earn their keep, which don't, what's missing
body:
# Deslop MCP tool-usage report from a long multi-agent dedup session

**Workspace:** NimblesiteAgenticPlatform/agent-backend (Python, ~26k LOC, ~100 files)
**Session result:** 211 fix points shipped, 639 → 381 clusters (40% reduction), 21.3% → 18.4% duplication
**Tools available:** mcp__deslop__{top-offenders, report-query, report-for-file, report-for-range, report-get, session-config, cluster-by-id, find-similar, list-embedding-models, set-embedding-model, rescan}

---

## ✅ Tools that earned their keep

### \`top-offenders\`
**Used:** 30+ times. Primary navigation entry point. Worked well once \`rescan\` shipped.
**Doc:** good — \"start here, one call gives everything\" is accurate.
**Issue resolved:** previously returned stale byte ranges (#78); fixed by \`rescan\`.

### \`report-query\` (filtered)
**Used:** 15+ times. Critical for: \`bucket=identical min_size=35\` to find real duplicates vs FPs. \`path_contains=test_X.py\` to scope to a file. \`bucket=same_behavior\` to surface AI-detected Type-4 hits.
**Doc:** good — filter list is clear.
**Best feature:** the \`metrics.duplication_percent\` in the response is the only honest progress signal during a multi-agent session. Should be highlighted more prominently.

### \`report-for-file\`
**Used:** 8 times. Shows all clusters touching a path with full occurrence byte ranges. Essential when planning a refactor that touches one file.
**Issue:** large files (e.g. test_sandbox_coverage.py) overflow context — saved to file with \"read it sequentially\" prompt. **The saved-file fallback is BRILLIANT** — kept me unblocked, would otherwise have lost the data. Highlight this in docs.

### \`session-config\`
**Used:** 5 times. Critical for diagnosing the \`incremental: false\` bug (#81). Without it I would have spent the whole session blaming my own changes for invisibility.
**Doc:** good. Flag \`incremental\` was the key signal.

### \`rescan\` (just shipped)
**Used:** 5 times. **Single most impactful new tool of this session.** Took deslop from \"silently stale\" to \"interactive\". Cluster count visibly dropped after each refactor.
**Doc:** ship-ready. The \`paths\` param to scope the rescan is clutch when you only touched 2 files.
**Suggestion:** mention in docs that calling without \`paths\` does a full reload — useful when a multi-file edit is committed at once.

---

## ❌ Tools I never invoked (review for removal)

### \`cluster-by-id\`
Never called. Reason: \`top-offenders\` and \`report-query\` already include enough cluster detail (occurrences, signals, summary). Calling \`cluster-by-id\` would be a strict subset of what those return.
**Verdict:** keep if used by hover bubble UI; agents don't need it.

### \`find-similar\`
Never called. Reason: when I have a code range that's duplicated I want to find OTHER duplicates of it — but \`top-offenders\` / \`report-query\` already cluster all duplicates together. Unclear what \`find-similar\` adds beyond the existing clustering.
**Verdict:** doc unclear. Either delete or write a doc example showing why it differs from \`report-query\`.

### \`report-for-range\`
Never called. Reason: I either want all clusters in a file (\`report-for-file\`) or all clusters in the project (\`report-query\`). A byte-range slice didn't come up.
**Verdict:** keep for hover-bubble use case; agents don't need it.

### \`report-get\`
Never called. Reason: too generic — when would you call this instead of \`top-offenders\`? Doc should clarify.
**Verdict:** doc unclear, likely redundant.

### \`list-embedding-models\` / \`set-embedding-model\`
Never called. Reason: never had reason to switch models mid-session. The currently active model showed up in \`embedding_provenance\` of every report response, which was sufficient.
**Verdict:** keep; CLI / config use case, not agent use case.

---

## 🐛 Tool issues encountered (highest pain first)

1. **session-config.incremental=false on file edits** (#81) → fixed by \`rescan\`. ✅
2. **top-offenders returned stale byte offsets** (#78) → fixed by \`rescan\`. ✅
3. **Helper-call sites flagged as Type-2 clones** (#79). Open. After dedup, the helper-call sites form their own cluster — and there's no way to fix them further without un-deduping.
4. **Parametric enum-value invariant tests flagged** (#97). Open.
5. **Test fixture dict variation flagged at structural=0.15** (#70). Open.
6. **Chained-dict-access assertions across unrelated tests** (#107). Just filed.
7. **\`report-for-file\` JSON over context limit** — the saved-file fallback works but is a workaround. Could be solved by adding pagination to the response (\`limit\` / \`offset\`) like \`report-query\` has.

---

## 📚 Docs: what's good, what needs fixing

**Good:**
- \`top-offenders\` ranking explanation with weight formula.
- The big embedded \`schema_doc\` that ships with every response. Saves an LLM from guessing \`structural\` vs \`token_jaccard\` semantics.
- \`bucket\` definitions tied to academic Type-1/2/3/4 clone categories.

**Needs work:**
- Pick one: does \`structural=1.0 token_jaccard=1.0\` always mean \"safe to extract\"? In practice: NO when occurrences are helper-call sites with literal-only differences. The doc says \"safe to extract\" without that caveat.
- The \`schema_doc\` repeats verbatim in every JSON response (~30k chars). Truncate or move to a separate \`mcp__deslop__schema-doc\` tool. Right now it eats agent context.
- No doc explains when to use \`find-similar\` vs \`report-query\` (see above).
- No doc on what \`cache_stats.hits / .misses\` mean — useful debugging signal but cryptic.
- No top-of-doc guide on \"first-time-using-deslop\" workflow. Suggested: top-offenders → pick #1 → report-for-file → fix → rescan.

---

## 🚀 Suggestions for new tools / features

1. **\`acknowledge-cluster\`** — mark a cluster as \"reviewed, intentionally divergent\" (e.g. parametric enum tests) so it stops appearing in top-offenders. Right now I have to file GH FP issues for each FP class, but the panel still shows them.
2. **\`extract-helper\` (codegen)** — given a cluster ID, generate the function signature for a candidate helper based on the variable parts across occurrences. Would speed up the \"name a helper\" step.
3. **\`progress\`** — a delta endpoint: \"clusters fixed since timestamp X\". Multi-agent sessions need this to show real progress.
4. **Truncate \`schema_doc\`** in MCP responses by default; opt in via param. Currently bloats context.

---

## Bottom-line takeaway

The 5 tools I actually used (\`top-offenders\`, \`report-query\`, \`report-for-file\`, \`session-config\`, \`rescan\`) form a coherent agent-driven dedup workflow. The other 6 are either UI-internals or never-explained. Trim those, polish docs on the 5 keepers, and add an \`acknowledge-cluster\` for FP suppression.

Filed alongside #78, #79, #81, #89, #92, #97, #107 from this same session.

title: pytest patterns (monkeypatch.setenv chains, assert dict-access chains, fixture call-sites) cluster as duplication
body:
## TL;DR

Deslop reports normal test code as duplicates. On a Python repo full of pytest tests, once the real copy-paste duplicates are dealt with, most of the top findings are everyday test patterns — repeated environment-variable setup, repeated assertion lines, and calls to helper functions the test author already created. They are not real duplicates, and they bury the genuine ones.

## Details

Deslop was run on a large Python project (NimblesiteAgenticPlatform). The real duplicated code across modules was cleaned up. After that, about 85% of the biggest remaining findings were in the test folder — and almost all of them were normal pytest patterns, not copies.

Four patterns show up again and again:

1. **Environment setup.** Many tests start by setting the same environment variables with `monkeypatch.setenv(...)` and then loading the config. The values differ per test; only the shape repeats.
2. **Lines of checks.** Tests deliberately check many fields one line at a time: `assert row["name"] == "tn-1"`, `assert row["content"] == ...`. The project's own guidelines ask for tests like this. Deslop sees the repeated shape and calls it a copy.
3. **Helper calls.** The test author already did the right thing — they moved shared code into a helper function. But every test calls that helper, and Deslop groups those calls as duplicates. The dedup was already done; grouping the calls again is wrong.
4. **Config blocks.** Big nested dictionaries for test setups look alike because they are all "settings", but their contents are different.

Why this matters: a user trying to get the duplication percentage down looks at this report, sees "duplicates" that clearly aren't, and stops trusting the tool.

Possible fixes (details for these are in the AI section below): stop reporting these patterns inside test files; or put test-code findings in their own hidden-by-default section of the report; or rank them much lower.

## Steps To Reproduce

1. Clone a pytest-heavy Python repository (the corpus above, or any project whose tests use `monkeypatch`, dense assertions, and shared helpers).
2. Run the scan: `deslop . --output /tmp/deslop`
3. Open `/tmp/deslop-report.html`.
4. Fix or ignore the genuine duplicated code in the top findings, then look at what remains at the top.
5. Observe: the biggest remaining findings are the four test patterns above — same-shaped setup code, assertion lines, and helper calls — flagged as duplicates.

## Details (for AI)

```shell
# evidence — the five false-positive clusters (same agent run over the corpus)
cluster id             copies  nodes  weight  structural  token_jaccard
9e0872770f874d0b       9       34     2830    1.00        1.00          # monkeypatch.setenv chain (worst offender)
82bebe84211f5b93       5       34     1208    1.00        1.00          # assert dict[key] == value chain
fc88c0f8fcc6e946       4       39     1131    1.00        1.00          # private-helper call site (_post_turn)
df3a03b38e612e29       4       38     1122    1.00        1.00          # private-helper call site
0e15b8e1d0e362e3       4       82     1600    0.15        0.97          # dict-literal fixtures (structural=0.15 is the tell)

# pattern shapes
1. monkeypatch.setenv chain:
   monkeypatch.setenv("FLY_API_TOKEN", "abc"); monkeypatch.delenv("FLY_APP_NAME", raising=False); ...; cfg = _load_config_from_env()
   -> different env-var sets per test; a parametrize matrix would obscure per-test acceptance; per-test helpers = one helper per test, no net win
2. assert subscript == literal chains over a single Name (row_r["tool_call_id"] == "id-1", ...) — deliberate assertion density per the project's AGENTS.md
3. call expressions to already-extracted private helpers (await _post_turn(client, test_api_key, config_id=..., message=..., conversation_id=None)) — the author already deduped; wrapping the wrapper is over-abstraction
4. nested dict literals (sandbox-config payload, PATCH body, httpx mock-handler trees) — token jaccard catches nested-dict-of-strings shape; AST shapes don't match (structural=0.15)

# context
corpus: NimblesiteAgenticPlatform src/ + tests/
share of weight>1000 clusters after genuine clones deduped: ~85% in tests/
related issues: #93 (embedding pass weak) #95 (Python generated suffixes) #96 (__all__ boilerplate)

# proposal options (pick one)
A. extend module-prologue boilerplate filter inside test files (test_*.py, *_test.py, tests/, __test__/):
   - Attribute(value=Name(id="monkeypatch"), attr="setenv"|"delenv") Call statement sequences
   - Assert(test=Compare(left=Subscript(...))) sequences over a single Name
   - call expressions whose target name starts with "_"
   (runs only on candidate ranges already filed under the cluster — bounded cost)
B. separate `test_pattern` bucket (alongside Identical/NearlyIdentical/LooselySimilar/SameBehavior), hidden by default, opt-in via --show-test-patterns
C. weight multiplier 0.25 for clusters with >=80% of occurrences in test files — pushes them down without hiding
preference: B (explicit, discoverable, no prod-code behavior change)
```

## Acceptance Criteria (for AI)

- New E2E fixture: a Python repo with the four pattern shapes above plus one genuinely refactorable cross-module clone.
- The genuinely refactorable clone surfaces at #1.
- The four test-pattern clusters are either hidden (Option A/B) or weight-penalised below the genuine clone (Option C).
- A report with **no** test-pattern matches looks identical (no false suppressions of prod-code clones).

## Screenshots

None.

title: False positive: same HTTP verb + status assertion across different endpoints
body:
## Summary

Cluster **10e21c4d0874fc34** (8 copies) flags the HTTP DELETE + 204 assertion pattern as duplicate code:

```python
resp = await client.delete(
    f"/api/v1/tenants/{tenant.id}",
    headers={"X-API-Key": test_api_key},
)
assert resp.status_code == 204
```

```python
resp = await client.delete(
    f"/api/v1/configs/{agent_config.id}",
    headers={"X-API-Key": test_api_key},
)
assert resp.status_code == 204
```

## Why it's a false positive

After identifier normalisation, both look identical: `client.delete(f"string/{X.Y}", headers={...})` + `assert resp.status_code == int`. But the endpoints are **different resources** being tested independently — `/tenants/` and `/configs/`. There is no extraction that would improve these tests; a `assert_delete_204(client, url, api_key)` helper would obscure what's actually being tested.

## Suggestion

REST endpoint tests naturally share the HTTP method + status pattern. Consider a heuristic: if the f-string template differs, the calls are testing different routes and should not be clustered as duplicates.

title: Autofix — AI-assisted Extract Method for Type-2 / Type-3 (MCP tool pair, not a code action)
body:
## Goal

Ship two new MCP tools — `extract-method-plan` and `extract-method-apply` — that handle Type-2 (renamed identifiers) and slot-alignable Type-3 (small structural drift) clusters by combining a **mechanical AST-derived scaffold** with a **tightly bounded AI fill**. The AI never writes code; it picks **one method name** and **one canonical name per parameter slot**. Deslop synthesises the final `WorkspaceEdit` deterministically from the scaffold + the AI's chosen names.

This is intentionally **not** a generic LSP `textDocument/codeAction` and **not** a generic file-edit. It's a specific MCP tool pair so the AI's freedom is bounded to named placeholder slots and never escapes into arbitrary text.

## Spec and plan

- **Spec:** [`docs/specs/autofix-extract.md` §[AUTOFIX-EXTRACT-AI]](docs/specs/autofix-extract.md#autofix-extract-ai-ai-assisted-extraction-for-type-2-and-type-3) — same spec doc as the Type-1 work; the AI path is its own section block. Sub-IDs: `[AUTOFIX-EXTRACT-AI-NORTH-STAR]`, `[AUTOFIX-EXTRACT-AI-SCAFFOLD]`, `[AUTOFIX-EXTRACT-AI-MCP-TOOLS]`, `[AUTOFIX-EXTRACT-AI-PRECONDITIONS]`, `[AUTOFIX-EXTRACT-AI-VALIDATION]`, `[AUTOFIX-EXTRACT-AI-NON-GOALS]`, `[AUTOFIX-EXTRACT-AI-DEPENDENCIES]`.
- **Plan:** [`docs/plans/autofix-extract-ai-plan.md`](docs/plans/autofix-extract-ai-plan.md) — phased implementation reusing the Type-1 emitter scaffolding, MCP wiring, language-by-language rollout, Type-3 admission as the final phase.

## Why MCP tool pair, not a code action

Code actions are synchronous; an AI round-trip is not. A `textDocument/codeAction` that blocks on an LLM call would freeze the editor. The MCP path lets the host agent (Claude Code, Cursor, Continue) drive the round-trip on its own schedule, then apply the returned `WorkspaceEdit` through its normal edit channel.

A future deferred code action could trigger the agent through the host's MCP client, but the canonical surface is the tool pair.

## Mechanical vs AI split — the load-bearing design choice

**Mechanical (always, AST-driven):**

- Cluster selection (already done by the pipeline).
- Per-occurrence free-variable extraction.
- Parameter-slot inference — site A's `customer` and site B's `admin` map to the same slot because they sit at the same source position in the normalised AST.
- Body skeleton with `__deslop_param_<i>` placeholders.
- Per-site call-site argument lists.
- Destination policy.
- Final `WorkspaceEdit` synthesis.

**AI-filled (non-deterministic, bounded slots):**

- One method name.
- One canonical name per parameter slot — chosen from the M candidates or generalising (`customer` + `admin` → `entity`).
- Optional one-line summary doc-comment.

That's it. The AI doesn't choose what to extract, doesn't modify the body, doesn't pick the destination, doesn't see the surrounding file beyond the scaffold, and doesn't generate file edits. Every AI input passes through [AUTOFIX-EXTRACT-AI-VALIDATION] before any edit is synthesised.

## Acceptance

- `extract-method-plan` returns the JSON scaffold for any Type-2 / slot-alignable Type-3 cluster.
- `extract-method-apply` validates AI-supplied names per [AUTOFIX-EXTRACT-AI-VALIDATION] and returns a `WorkspaceEdit` byte-for-byte deterministic for the same inputs.
- `extract-method-apply` rejects invalid identifiers, name collisions, arity mismatches, and duplicates with a typed error and a redux of the scaffold so the agent can retry without re-fetching.
- C#, Rust, and Python all covered by golden E2E tests against the real `deslop-mcp` binary.
- Type-3 clusters whose occurrences differ in free-variable arity are correctly skipped (no scaffold returned).
- Tool descriptions follow [MCP-AGENT-PROMPT-GUIDANCE] — phrased so a host agent picks them up correctly.

## Hard dependencies

1. **Type-1 path** ([#43](https://github.com/Nimblesite/Deslop/issues/43)) lands first. The slot-substitution layer extends the same emitter rather than forking it.
2. **Issue [#42](https://github.com/Nimblesite/Deslop/issues/42)** — `kind_detail` Type-1 vs Type-2 split must exist; the AI path's eligibility check reads it.
3. `LanguageParser::align_slots(occurrences) -> Option<SlotMapping>` — same single extension point as parsing and Type-1 free-vars.

## Out of scope (v1)

- AI-generated body code.
- AI-chosen destination.
- AI-driven type inference.
- Cross-file or cross-class extraction.
- A "freeform extract" tool that accepts arbitrary code from the agent.
- LSP code action surface (deferred; canonical surface is the MCP tool pair).

title: Investigate + extract shared logic between pipeline/session.rs and live/session.rs
body:
## Summary

Deslop's own report flags large near-identical regions inside **both** [crates/deslop-core/src/pipeline/session.rs](crates/deslop-core/src/pipeline/session.rs) (499 LOC) and [crates/deslop-core/src/live/session.rs](crates/deslop-core/src/live/session.rs) (449 LOC). The top-level clusters are intra-file sibling-extension artifacts (tracked separately in #21), but the secondary signal is strong: two similarly-named session files, each with a ~1.5k-node contiguous flagged region, and dozens of smaller same-file clusters scattered between them.

This is a **cleanup TODO**, not a deslop bug. Extracting the shared pieces would simultaneously shrink both files below the 500-line hard rule (pipeline/session.rs is already at 499) and dogfood the tool on its own codebase.

## Evidence from `report-query path_contains=session.rs`

Each file has one large self-similar block:

- `pipeline/session.rs`: cluster `6fb3131f2595168e`, 1671 nodes, bytes 4384–18402
- `live/session.rs`: cluster `d2f416fb0f3b803d`, 1508 nodes, bytes 2554–15686

Plus ~30 smaller clusters spread across both files (clusters `1963e435df4dd282`, `3e94b84cb8beed80`, `496d67e1f0ac5ff7`, `2aef0482f9eecaf2`, `961605958781fc99`, `2e645d115a89b709`, `1b000733bf2e729d`, `02376efe17b4f18f`, … — 34 in total from `path_contains=session.rs`).

## Hypothesis

`live::Session` and `pipeline::Session` implement the same pipeline stages (discover → parse → normalize → fingerprint → cluster → rank → render) with different orchestration — live is incremental, batch is one-shot. The per-stage invocation, state wiring, and result plumbing is likely near-identical.

## Suggested approach

1. Open both files side by side. Identify the shared stage sequence.
2. Pull the common stage-driver into a `SessionCore` (or trait) in a new module under `crates/deslop-core/src/` — keep global state in [crates/deslop-core/src/state.rs](crates/deslop-core/src/state.rs) per CLAUDE.md.
3. `live::Session` and `pipeline::Session` become thin wrappers that only differ in their incremental vs. batch behavior.
4. Re-run deslop and verify the flagged regions shrink (both absolute node counts and the overall `duplication_percent`).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Both files drop below ~300 LOC (currently 499 and 449).
- [ ] `make test` passes with no coverage regression.
- [ ] Deslop rerun on this repo no longer shows 1.5k+ node near-identical blocks in either session file (some residue is fine; the huge contiguous block should be gone).
- [ ] No new `#[allow(...)]`, no new `unwrap`/`expect` — CLAUDE.md hard rules stand.

## Blocked by / related

- #21 — the sibling-extension ranking false-positive. Fixing #21 first will sharpen this report: once intra-file overlaps are collapsed, whatever residual cross-file signal exists between these two files will surface directly.

title: VSIX tree context menu: Ignore This Duplicate
body:
## Summary

Add a context-menu item for suppressing a noisy duplicate finding from the tree.

## Applies to

- `deslop.cluster` tree nodes.
- `deslop.occurrence` tree nodes.

## Behavior

The command should help the user ignore either:

- the selected occurrence path/range;
- the whole cluster;
- or the file/path pattern, depending on what the existing exclusion model supports.

If persistence requires editing `.deslop.toml`, show the exact rule before applying it.

## Acceptance criteria

- Context menu item title: `Ignore This Duplicate`.
- Does not silently mutate config; prompts with the rule/action first.
- Refreshes the report after the ignore action is applied.
- Keeps AI/report output semantics clear: ignored UI items should not masquerade as deleted code.
- Tests cover command availability and the generated suppression payload/rule.
